ukberi-tibyan:32-32.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ وَلَلدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ) (٣٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَلدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ): it is read with the alif and lām, with الْآخِرَةُ in the nominative as a naʿt (adjective); and the khabar (predicate) is «خَيْرٌ».
It is also read «وَلَدَارُ الْآخِرَةِ» as a genitive construct (iḍāfa); i.e. "the abode of the Last Hour". The abode is not put in construct with its own adjective, because the adjective is the same as the thing described in meaning, and a thing is not put in construct with itself; but the Kufans permitted it.

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَدْ نَعْلَمُ إِنَّهُ لَيَحْزُنُكَ الَّذِي يَقُولُونَ فَإِنَّهُمْ لَا يُكَذِّبُونَكَ وَلَكِنَّ الظَّالِمِينَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ يَجْحَدُونَ) (٣٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَدْ نَعْلَمُ): i.e. "We have known"; so the imperfect has the meaning of the past.
(لَا يُكَذِّبُونَكَ): it is read with shadda, in the sense "they do not ascribe lying to you", i.e. before your claim to prophethood; rather they used to know him for trustworthiness and truthfulness. It is also read without shadda, and in it there are two views. One of them: it has the meaning of the shadda form; one says أَكْذَبْتُهُ and كَذَّبْتُهُ when you ascribe lying to him.
The second: "they do not find you a liar"; one says أَكْذَبْتُهُ when you find him so, as when you say أَحْمَدْتُهُ when you find him praiseworthy. (بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ): the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (يَجْحَدُونَ). It is also said: it is attached to الظَّالِمِينَ, as in His saying, Exalted is He: (وَآتَيْنَا ثَمُودَ النَّاقَةَ مُبْصِرَةً فَظَلَمُوا بِهَا).

ukberi-tibyan:34-34.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ كُذِّبَتْ رُسُلٌ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ فَصَبَرُوا عَلَى مَا كُذِّبُوا وَأُوذُوا حَتَّى أَتَاهُمْ نَصْرُنَا وَلَا مُبَدِّلَ لِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ وَلَقَدْ جَاءَكَ مِنْ نَبَأِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ) (٣٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ قَبْلِكَ): it may not be a naʿt (adjective) of رُسُلٍ, because it is a time expression, and a corporeal being (al-juththa) is not described by time; it is only attached (mutaʿalliq) to كُذِّبَتْ. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «وَالْجَنَّةُ» ("the Garden"), evidently a misprint for «وَالْجُثَّةُ» ("a corporeal being"); translated according to the evident sense.] (وَأُوذُوا): it may be maʿṭūf (conjoined) to كُذِّبُوا, so that «حَتَّى» is attached to صَبَرُوا.
It may also be that the pause is complete at كُذِّبُوا, and then He began anew and said: وَأُوذُوا, so that حَتَّى is attached to it; but the first is stronger. (وَلَقَدْ جَاءَكَ): the fāʿil (agent) of جَاءَكَ is a pronoun implied in it. It is said: the implied element is "the coming"; and it is said: the implied element is "the news", indicated by the mention of the messengers, because a message is a necessary concomitant of a messenger, and it is news. On both views «مِنْ نَبَأِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun, the implied sense being "of the kind of the news of the messengers".
Al-Akhfash permitted مِنْ to be redundant (zāʾida), with the agent being نَبَأُ الْمُرْسَلِينَ; but Sībawayh does not permit its redundancy in an affirmative statement (al-wājib). And according to all, it is not permissible for مِنْ to be the naʿt of something omitted, because the agent is not omitted, and a preposition that is not redundant cannot properly be an agent, since a preposition is a means of making a verb transitive, and every verb governs its agent without any such means. And (نَبَأِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ) means "the informing about them"; this is shown by His saying, Exalted is He: (نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الرُّسُلِ).

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنْ كَانَ كَبُرَ عَلَيْكَ إِعْرَاضُهُمْ فَإِنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ أَنْ تَبْتَغِيَ نَفَقًا فِي الْأَرْضِ أَوْ سُلَّمًا فِي السَّمَاءِ فَتَأْتِيَهُمْ بِآيَةٍ وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَجَمَعَهُمْ عَلَى الْهُدَى فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْجَاهِلِينَ) (٣٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِنْ كَانَ كَبُرَ عَلَيْكَ): the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of this «إِنْ» is (فَإِنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ); so the second conditional is the apodosis of the first, and the apodosis of the second conditional is omitted, its implied form being "then do it"; it was omitted because its meaning is evident and the sentence is long. (فِي الْأَرْضِ): a naʿt (adjective) of نَفَقٍ; it may also be attached (mutaʿalliq) to تَبْتَغِي.
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun, i.e. "while you are in the earth"; and likewise «فِي السَّمَاءِ».

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّمَا يَسْتَجِيبُ الَّذِينَ يَسْمَعُونَ وَالْمَوْتَى يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُونَ) (٣٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالْمَوْتَى يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ): there are two views on الْمَوْتَى:
One of them: it is in the position of the accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "and Allah will raise the dead"; and this is stronger, because it is a noun conjoined to a noun on which a verb has operated. The second: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what follows it is the khabar (predicate); and يَسْتَجِيبُ has the meaning of يُجِيبُ.

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالُوا لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ قُلْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَادِرٌ عَلَى أَنْ يُنَزِّلَ آيَةً وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ) (٣٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ رَبِّهِ): it may be a naʿt (adjective) of آيَةٌ, or it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to نُزِّلَ.

ukberi-tibyan:38-38.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا مِنْ دَابَّةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا طَائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ إِلَّا أُمَمٌ أَمْثَالُكُمْ مَا فَرَّطْنَا فِي الْكِتَابِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ ثُمَّ إِلَى رَبِّهِمْ يُحْشَرُونَ) (٣٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي الْأَرْضِ): it may be in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of دَابَّةٍ, and also in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of it according to its position, because مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida). (وَلَا طَائِرٍ): maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the wording of دَابَّةٍ; and it has been read in the nominative according to the position. (بِجَنَاحَيْهِ): the bāʾ may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to يَطِيرُ, or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial); and it is tawkīd (emphasis), and in it is a removal of figurative use, because of something other than a bird it may be said "it flew" when it hastened. (مِنْ شَيْءٍ): «مِنْ» is redundant; and «شَيْءٌ» here stands in the place of the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "any neglect"; on this interpretation no proof remains in the verse for whoever supposed that the Book contains explicit mention of every thing.
Its parallel is (لَا يَضُرُّكُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْئًا), i.e. "any harm"; and we have mentioned parallels to it.
It is not permissible for «شَيْئًا» to be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because فَرَّطْنَا is not transitive by itself but only by means of a preposition, and it has already been made transitive by فِي to الْكِتَابِ, so it is not made transitive by another preposition. Nor is it sound for the meaning to be "We have not left out anything in the Book", because the meaning is otherwise; so it is clear that the interpretation is what we have mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا صُمٌّ وَبُكْمٌ فِي الظُّلُمَاتِ مَنْ يَشَأِ اللَّهُ يُضْلِلْهُ وَمَنْ يَشَأْ يَجْعَلْهُ عَلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ) (٣٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا): mubtadaʾ (subject), and (صُمٌّ وَبُكْمٌ) is the khabar (predicate), like حُلْوٌ حَامِضٌ ("sweet-sour"); and the wāw does not prevent that.
It may also be that «صُمٌّ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "some of them are deaf and some of them are dumb".
(فِي الظُّلُمَاتِ): it may be a second khabar, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun implied in the khabar, the implied sense being "straying in the darknesses".
It may also be that فِي الظُّلُمَاتِ is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are in the darknesses".
It may also be a naʿt (adjective) of بُكْمٌ, i.e. "being in the darknesses"; and it may be an adverbial (ẓarf) of صُمٌّ or بُكْمٌ, or of the verb that stands in for them.
(مَنْ يَشَأِ اللَّهُ): مَنْ is in the position of a mubtadaʾ, and the apodosis (jawāb) is the khabar. It may also be in the position of the accusative by an omitted verb, because the implied sense is "whomever Allah wills his being led astray, or his punishment"; so what is made accusative by «يَشَأْ» is something connected with «مَنْ», and the implied sense becomes "whomever He punishes" or "whomever He leads astray"; and likewise what follows it.

ukberi-tibyan:40-40.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ أَرَأَيْتَكُمْ إِنْ أَتَاكُمْ عَذَابُ اللَّهِ أَوْ أَتَتْكُمُ السَّاعَةُ أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ تَدْعُونَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ) (٤٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قُلْ أَرَأَيْتَكُمْ): it is read with the vowel of the hamza cast onto the lām, so the lām takes fatḥa and the hamza is dropped; this is a regular analogical rule in the Quran and elsewhere, and its purpose is lightening.
It is also read with full pronunciation (taḥqīq) of the hamza, which is the original. As for the hamza after the rāʾ, it is pronounced fully according to the original, softened for lightening, and dropped. The way of that is that it is changed into a yāʾ, made vowelless, and then dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters; what made that easier in it is its dropping in the imperfect of this verb.
As for the tāʾ, it is the agent pronoun. When the kāf of address is attached to it, it has one form in the dual, the plural and the feminine, and these meanings are distinguished on the kāf. So you say for the singular أَرَأَيْتَكَ, and from it is His saying, Exalted is He: (أَرَأَيْتَكَ هَذَا الَّذِي كَرَّمْتَ عَلَيَّ); for the dual أَرَأَيْتَكُمَا; for the plural أَرَأَيْتَكُمْ; and for the feminine أَرَأَيْتَكُنَّ; and the tāʾ in all of that has fatḥa.
The kāf is a particle of address, not a noun. The proof of that is that if it were a noun, it would be either genitive, which is false since there is nothing governing the genitive here; or nominative, which is also false for two reasons: one of them, that the kāf is not among the nominative pronouns.
The second: that there is nothing to make it nominative, since it is not a fāʿil (agent), because the tāʾ is the agent, and one verb does not have two agents. Or it would be accusative, and that is false for three reasons:
First: this verb is transitive to two objects, as when you say أَرَأَيْتَ زَيْدًا مَا فَعَلَ ("Have you considered Zayd, what he did?"); so if you made the kāf an object, it would be a third. Second: if it were an object, it would be the same as the agent in meaning, and the meaning is not that, since the intent is not "have you seen yourself?" but "have you seen someone other than you?"; for that reason you said أَرَأَيْتَكَ زَيْدًا, and Zayd is other than the one addressed, nor is he a badal (substitute) of him. Third: if it were accusative as an object, the marker of the dual, the plural and the feminine would appear on the tāʾ, and you would say أَرَأَيْتَمَاكُمَا, أَرَأَيْتَمُوكُمْ and أَرَأَيْتَكُنَّ. [Translator's note: the third form is printed thus in the source; by the argument one would expect أَرَأَيْتُنَّكُنَّ.]
Al-Farrāʾ held that the kāf is an accusative pronoun noun with the meaning of a nominative; and what we have mentioned refutes his position. As for the object of أَرَأَيْتَكُمْ in this verse, some said: it is omitted, the context indicating it, its implied form being "Have you considered your worship of the idols — will it benefit you when the Hour comes?"; and His saying «أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ تَدْعُونَ» indicates it.
Others said: this needs no object, because the conditional and its apodosis have yielded the meaning of the object. As for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the conditional, which is His saying «إِنْ أَتَاكُمْ عَذَابُ اللَّهِ», it is what is indicated by the interrogative in His saying «أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ», its implied form being "if the Hour comes upon you, you will call upon Allah".
«وَغَيْرَ» is accusative by «تَدْعُونَ».

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (بَلْ إِيَّاهُ تَدْعُونَ فَيَكْشِفُ مَا تَدْعُونَ إِلَيْهِ إِنْ شَاءَ وَتَنْسَوْنَ مَا تُشْرِكُونَ) (٤١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَلْ إِيَّاهُ): it is the object of the «تَدْعُونَ» that follows it.
(إِلَيْهِ): it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to تَدْعُونَ, or attached to يَكْشِفُ, i.e. "He lifts it to Himself".
And «مَا» means الَّذِي (that which), or is an indefinite noun described by what follows; it is not maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun) unless you make it a maṣdar with the meaning of the passive participle (the object).

ukberi-tibyan:42-42.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَى أُمَمٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ فَأَخَذْنَاهُمْ بِالْبَأْسَاءِ وَالضَّرَّاءِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَضَرَّعُونَ) (٤٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِالْبَأْسَاءِ وَالضَّرَّاءِ): the pattern faʿlāʾ in both is a feminine for which no masculine is used; they did not say بَأْسٌ and بَأْسَاءُ, or ضُرٌّ and ضَرَّاءُ, as they said أَحْمَرُ and حَمْرَاءُ. [Translator's note: the intended sense is that no masculine of the pattern afʿal (أَبْأَسُ / أَضَرُّ) is used for these, as أَحْمَرُ is for حَمْرَاءُ.]

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَوْلَا إِذْ جَاءَهُمْ بَأْسُنَا تَضَرَّعُوا وَلَكِنْ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ) (٤٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَلَوْلَا إِذْ): «إِذْ» is in the position of the accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf) of «تَضَرَّعُوا», i.e. "why then did they not humble themselves when…". (وَلَكِنْ): a correction (istidrāk) based on the meaning, i.e. "they did not humble themselves, but…".

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا نَسُوا مَا ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ فَتَحْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ أَبْوَابَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَتَّى إِذَا فَرِحُوا بِمَا أُوتُوا أَخَذْنَاهُمْ بَغْتَةً فَإِذَا هُمْ مُبْلِسُونَ) (٤٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَغْتَةً): a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent, i.e. "taking them by surprise", or from the objects, or "taken by surprise". [Translator's note: the text reads «أَوْ مِنَ الْمَفْعُولَيْنِ أَوْ مَبْغُوتِينَ»; the second «أَوْ» is probably for «أَيْ», giving "or from the objects, i.e. taken by surprise".]
It may also be a maṣdar according to the meaning, because أَخَذْنَاهُمْ means "We surprised them".
(فَإِذَا هُمْ): إِذَا here is for sudden occurrence (mufājaʾa), and it is an adverb of place; هُمْ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (مُبْلِسُونَ) is its khabar (predicate), and it is what governs إِذَا.

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ سَمْعَكُمْ وَأَبْصَارَكُمْ وَخَتَمَ عَلَى قُلُوبِكُمْ مَنْ إِلَهٌ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ يَأْتِيكُمْ بِهِ انْظُرْ كَيْفَ نُصَرِّفُ الْآيَاتِ ثُمَّ هُمْ يَصْدِفُونَ) (٤٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ سَمْعَكُمْ): we have mentioned the reason for the singular of السَّمْع alongside the plural of الْأَبْصَار and الْقُلُوب at the beginning of al-Baqara. (مَنْ): an interrogative in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (إِلَهٌ) is its khabar (predicate), and (غَيْرُ اللَّهِ) is a naʿt (adjective) of the khabar. And (يَأْتِيَكُمُ) is also in the position of a naʿt; and the interrogative here has the meaning of denial (inkār). [Translator's note: the word is printed «يَأْتِيَكُمُ» in the source; the verse reads «يَأْتِيكُمْ».]
The hāʾ in «بِهِ» refers back to السَّمْع, because it is what is mentioned first. It is also said: it refers to the sense of "what is taken and sealed", and therefore it is singular. «كَيْفَ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and what governs it is «نُصَرِّفُ».

ukberi-tibyan:47-47.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ أَرَأَيْتَكُمْ إِنْ أَتَاكُمْ عَذَابُ اللَّهِ بَغْتَةً أَوْ جَهْرَةً هَلْ يُهْلَكُ إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الظَّالِمُونَ) (٤٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هَلْ يُهْلَكُ): the interrogative here has the meaning of affirmation (taqrīr); therefore it stands in for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), i.e. "if it comes upon you, you will perish".

ukberi-tibyan:48-48.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا نُرْسِلُ الْمُرْسَلِينَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنْذِرِينَ فَمَنْ آمَنَ وَأَصْلَحَ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ) (٤٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنْذِرِينَ): two ḥāls (circumstantials) from الْمُرْسَلِينَ.
(فَمَنْ آمَنَ): it may be conditional, or it may mean الَّذِي (the one who); in both cases it is a mubtadaʾ (subject); and the discussion of its parallels has preceded.

ukberi-tibyan:49-49.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا يَمَسُّهُمُ الْعَذَابُ بِمَا كَانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ) (٤٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِمَا كَانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ): مَا is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), i.e. "because of their transgression"; it was mentioned near the beginning of al-Baqara. It is read with ḍamma on the sīn and with kasra, and they are two dialectal forms.

ukberi-tibyan:109-109.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ لَئِنْ جَاءَتْهُمْ آيَةٌ لَيُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهَا قُلْ إِنَّمَا الْآيَاتُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَمَا يُشْعِرُكُمْ أَنَّهَا إِذَا جَاءَتْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ) (109).
His saying (جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ): this has been discussed in al-Māʾida.
(وَمَا يُشْعِرُكُمْ): «مَا» is interrogative, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and يُشْعِرُكُمْ is the khabar (predicate); it is transitive to two objects.
(أَنَّهَا): it is read with kasra (إِنَّهَا) as a resumptive (new) sentence, and the second object is omitted, its implied form being: "and what makes you aware of their believing?"
It is also read with fatḥa (أَنَّهَا), and on this there are three views. The first: that «أَنَّ» means «لَعَلَّ» ("perhaps"), which al-Khalīl reported from the Arabs; on this view the second object is likewise omitted.
The second: that «لَا» is redundant (zāʾida), so «أَنَّ» together with what it governs is in the position of the second object.
The third: that «أَنَّ» has its usual function and «لَا» is not redundant; the meaning is "and what makes you know of their not believing?" This is a reply to those who judged them to be disbelievers forever and despaired of their faith; the implied form is: "they will not believe in it," and the object was omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:110-110.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَنُقَلِّبُ أَفْئِدَتَهُمْ وَأَبْصَارَهُمْ كَمَا لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِهِ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَنَذَرُهُمْ فِي طُغْيَانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ) (110).
His saying (كَمَا لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا): «مَا» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and the kāf is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a turning like their disbelief," i.e. a punishment equal to their disobedience.
(أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ): an adverb of time; this has already been discussed. (وَنَذَرُهُمْ): it is read with nūn and ḍamma on the rāʾ, and with yāʾ (وَيَذَرُهُمْ) likewise; the meaning is clear.
It is also read with sukūn on the rāʾ (وَنَذَرْهُمْ), and on this there are two views. The first: that it was made quiescent because of the heaviness of successive vowels.
The second: that it is jussive (majzūm), conjoined to يُؤْمِنُوا; the meaning is "as a requital for their disbelief," and that He did not leave them wandering blindly in their transgression but rather made things clear to them.

ukberi-tibyan:111-111.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَوْ أَنَّنَا نَزَّلْنَا إِلَيْهِمُ الْمَلَائِكَةَ وَكَلَّمَهُمُ الْمَوْتَى وَحَشَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ قُبُلًا مَا كَانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ يَجْهَلُونَ) (111).
His saying (قُبُلًا): it is read with ḍamma on the qāf and the bāʾ, and there are two views on it. The first: it is the plural of قَبِيل ("group"), like قَلِيب and قُلُب. The second: that it is a singular, like the قُبُل ("front") of a person and his دُبُر ("back"). On both views it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «كُلَّ»; that is permitted, even though it is indefinite, because of the generality it contains.
It is also read with ḍamma and sukūn on the bāʾ (قُبْلًا), as a lightening of the ḍamma.
It is also read with kasra on the qāf and fatḥa on the bāʾ (قِبَلًا), and there are likewise two views on it. The first: it is an adverb, as when you say: لِي قِبَلَهُ حَقٌّ ("I have a claim on him"). The second: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. "openly" or "face to face."
(إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ): in the position of the accusative as a disconnected exception. It has also been said to be a connected exception, the meaning being: they would not believe in any state except in the state of Allah the Exalted willing it.

ukberi-tibyan:112-112.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَا لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ عَدُوًّا شَيَاطِينَ الْإِنْسِ وَالْجِنِّ يُوحِي بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَى بَعْضٍ زُخْرُفَ الْقَوْلِ غُرُورًا وَلَوْ شَاءَ رَبُّكَ مَا فَعَلُوهُ فَذَرْهُمْ وَمَا يَفْتَرُونَ) (112).
His saying (وَكَذَلِكَ): it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), as we have mentioned in more than one place.
(جَعَلْنَا): transitive to two objects. Regarding the first object there are two views. The first: it is «عَدُوًّا». The second: «لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ», and «شَيَاطِينَ» is a badal (substitute) of عَدُوّ.
The second: the first object is شَيَاطِينَ, and عَدُوًّا is the second object, placed first, and لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ is an adjective of عَدُوّ which was placed before it and so became a ḥāl (circumstantial). «[Translator's note: the source text's enumeration of the views is as given here; it is translated as written.]»
(يُوحِي): it may be a ḥāl of شَيَاطِينَ, or an adjective (ṣifa) of عَدُوّ, عَدُوّ standing in the place of أَعْدَاء ("enemies"). «[Translator's note: the printed text has صِلَةً ("relative clause") here; it is rendered in the sense of an adjective, but the source wording is صلة.]» (غُرُورًا): a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); it has also been said to be a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl. The hāʾ in (فَعَلُوهُ) may be the pronoun of the "inspiring," indicated by يُوحَى, or the pronoun of the زُخْرُف ("embellishment"), or of the قَوْل ("speech"), or of the غُرُور ("deception").
(وَمَا يَفْتَرُونَ): «مَا» means «الَّذِي» ("that which"), or is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, or is maṣdariyya; it is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the object before it. The wāw may also mean «مَعَ» ("with").

ukberi-tibyan:113-113.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلِتَصْغَى إِلَيْهِ أَفْئِدَةُ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ وَلِيَرْضَوْهُ وَلِيَقْتَرِفُوا مَا هُمْ مُقْتَرِفُونَ) (113).
His saying (وَلِتَصْغَى): the majority read it with kasra on the lām, and it is conjoined to «غُرُورًا», i.e. "in order to deceive and in order that … may incline."
It has also been said that it is the lām of the oath, given kasra because the verb was not made emphatic with the nūn.
It has been read with the lām made quiescent (وَلْتَصْغَى); it is lightened because of successive vowels, and it is not the lām of command, because the verb is not jussive. The same applies to «وَلِيَرْضَوْهُ وَلِيَقْتَرِفُوا».
«مَا» means «الَّذِي», and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "and that they may commit that which they are committing (مُقْتَرِفُوهُ)"; the nūn was retained when the hāʾ was omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:114-114.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَفَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَبْتَغِي حَكَمًا وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ إِلَيْكُمُ الْكِتَابَ مُفَصَّلًا وَالَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ يَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ مُنَزَّلٌ مِنْ رَبِّكَ بِالْحَقِّ فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُمْتَرِينَ) (114).
His saying (أَفَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ): there are two views on it. The first: it is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of أَبْتَغِي, and «حَكَمًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of it.
The second: that حَكَمًا is the object of أَبْتَغِي, and «غَيْرَ» is a ḥāl of حَكَمًا placed before it.
It has also been said that حَكَمًا is a tamyīz (specification).
(مُفَصَّلًا): a ḥāl of الْكِتَاب. (بِالْحَقِّ): a ḥāl of the nominative pronoun in «مُنَزَّلٌ».

ukberi-tibyan:115-115.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ صِدْقًا وَعَدْلًا لَا مُبَدِّلَ لِكَلِمَاتِهِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ) (115).
His saying (صِدْقًا وَعَدْلًا): both are accusative as tamyīz (specification). They may also be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(لَا مُبَدِّلَ): a resumptive (new) sentence. It may not be a ḥāl of رَبِّكَ, lest the ḥāl be separated from the one it describes by something extraneous, namely His saying «صِدْقًا وَعَدْلًا» — unless «صِدْقًا وَعَدْلًا» are made two ḥāls of رَبِّكَ, not of the كَلِمَات ("words").

ukberi-tibyan:117-117.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ مَنْ يَضِلُّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ) (117).
His saying (أَعْلَمُ مَنْ يَضِلُّ): regarding «مَنْ» there are two views. The first: it means «الَّذِي» ("the one who"), or is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, meaning "a group." On this view it is in the position of the accusative by a verb indicated by «أَعْلَمُ», not by «أَعْلَمُ» itself, because the afʿal pattern (elative) does not put an overt noun in the accusative; the implied form is: "He knows who goes astray." It is not permissible for «مَنْ» to be in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa) on the reading of those who read the yāʾ with fatḥa (يَضِلُّ), lest the implied meaning become "He is the most knowing of those who go astray," which would entail that He, glory be to Him, is among the astray — exalted is He above that.
For those who read with ḍamma on the yāʾ (يُضِلُّ), «مَنْ» is likewise in the position of the accusative as we have explained, i.e. "He knows those who lead astray." It may also be in the position of the genitive, either in the sense "He is the most knowing of those made astray (الْمُضَلِّينَ)," i.e. of one who finds them astray — from أَضْلَلْتُهُ, i.e. "I found him astray," like أَحْمَدْتُهُ, "I found him praiseworthy" — or in the sense that he goes astray from guidance.
The second view: that «مَنْ» is interrogative in the position of a mubtadaʾ (subject), «يَضِلُّ» is the khabar (predicate), and the position of the clause is accusative by the implied «يَعْلَمُ». Similar to it is: (لِنَعْلَمَ أَيُّ الْحِزْبَيْنِ أَحْصَى).

ukberi-tibyan:119-119.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا لَكُمْ أَلَّا تَأْكُلُوا مِمَّا ذُكِرَ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ وَقَدْ فَصَّلَ لَكُمْ مَا حَرَّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِلَّا مَا اضْطُرِرْتُمْ إِلَيْهِ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرًا لَيُضِلُّونَ بِأَهْوَائِهِمْ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُعْتَدِينَ) (119).
His saying (وَمَا لَكُمْ): «مَا» is interrogative, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and «لَكُمْ» is the khabar (predicate).
(أَلَّا تَأْكُلُوا): there are two views on it. The first: a preposition is intended with it, i.e. "in that you do not eat" (فِي أَنْ لَا تَأْكُلُوا); when the preposition was omitted it came to be in the position of the accusative, or in the position of the genitive, according to their disagreement on that. This has been mentioned in more than one place.
The second: that it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "what is the matter with you, refraining from eating?" This is weak, because «أَنْ» makes the verb purely future and turns it into a maṣdar (verbal noun), so the ḥāl is impossible — unless you assume the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being: "what is the matter with you, being people of not eating (ذَوِي أَنْ لَا تَأْكُلُوا)?" The object is omitted, i.e. "anything of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned."
(وَقَدْ فَصَّلَ): the clause is a ḥāl. It is read with ḍamma, as a passive verb (whose agent is not named), and with fatḥa, naming the agent; and with the ṣād doubled (فَصَّلَ) and undoubled (فَصَلَ). All of that is clear.
(إِلَّا مَا اضْطُرِرْتُمْ): «مَا» is in the position of the accusative as an exception from the same genus, by way of the meaning; for He rebuked them for refraining from eating what [Allah's name] was mentioned over, and that entails the permission to eat absolutely; and His saying «وَقَدْ فَصَّلَ لَكُمْ مَا حَرَّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ» means: in the state of free choice, while that is lawful in the state of necessity.

ukberi-tibyan:121-121.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا مِمَّا لَمْ يُذْكَرِ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ وَإِنَّهُ لَفِسْقٌ وَإِنَّ الشَّيَاطِينَ لَيُوحُونَ إِلَى أَوْلِيَائِهِمْ لِيُجَادِلُوكُمْ وَإِنْ أَطَعْتُمُوهُمْ إِنَّكُمْ لَمُشْرِكُونَ) (121).
His saying (إِنَّكُمْ لَمُشْرِكُونَ): the fāʾ has been omitted from the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). This is good when the condition is in the form of the past tense, and here it is so, namely His saying «وَإِنْ أَطَعْتُمُوهُمْ».

ukberi-tibyan:122-123.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَوَمَنْ كَانَ مَيْتًا فَأَحْيَيْنَاهُ وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُ نُورًا يَمْشِي بِهِ فِي النَّاسِ كَمَنْ مَثَلُهُ فِي الظُّلُمَاتِ لَيْسَ بِخَارِجٍ مِنْهَا كَذَلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِلْكَافِرِينَ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ (122) وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَا فِي كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ أَكَابِرَ مُجْرِمِيهَا لِيَمْكُرُوا فِيهَا وَمَا يَمْكُرُونَ إِلَّا بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ) (123).
His saying (أَوَمَنْ كَانَ): «مَنْ» means «الَّذِي» ("the one who"), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
(يَمْشِي بِهِ): in the position of the accusative as an adjective (ṣifa) of نُور. (كَمَنْ): the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. (مَثَلُهُ): a mubtadaʾ, and «فِي الظُّلُمَاتِ» is its khabar.
(لَيْسَ بِخَارِجٍ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in the preposition phrase. It may not be a ḥāl of the hāʾ in «مَثَلُهُ», because of the separation between it and the ḥāl by the khabar.
(كَذَلِكَ زُيِّنَ) and (كَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَا): their i'rab has preceded.
جَعَلْنَا means صَيَّرْنَا ("We made [to be]"). (أَكَابِرَ): the first object, and فِي كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ the second.
(مُجْرِمِيهَا): a badal (substitute) of أَكَابِرَ. It is also possible that «فِي» is an adverbial, مُجْرِمِيهَا the first object, and «أَكَابِرَ» the second object.
It is also possible that «أَكَابِرَ» is annexed (muḍāf) to «مُجْرِمِيهَا», and «فِي كُلِّ» is the second object; on this view the meaning is "We established (مَكَّنَّا)," or the like.
(لِيَمْكُرُوا): the lām is the lām of purpose (lām kay) or the lām of outcome (lām al-ṣayrūra).

ukberi-tibyan:124-124.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذَا جَاءَتْهُمْ آيَةٌ قَالُوا لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ حَتَّى نُؤْتَى مِثْلَ مَا أُوتِيَ رُسُلُ اللَّهِ اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ حَيْثُ يَجْعَلُ رِسَالَتَهُ سَيُصِيبُ الَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُوا صَغَارٌ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَعَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ بِمَا كَانُوا يَمْكُرُونَ) (124).
His saying (حَيْثُ يَجْعَلُ): حَيْثُ here is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the governing word is omitted, the implied form being: "He knows the place of His messages." It is not an adverbial, because the implied meaning would then become "He knows in this place such-and-such," and that is not the meaning. «حَيْثَ» has also been transmitted with fatḥa on the thāʾ; according to most it is an indeclinable (mabnī) ending, and it has also been said to be a declinable fatḥa (of i'rab).
(عِنْدَ اللَّهِ): an adverbial of «يُصِيبُ», or an adjective of صَغَارٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:125-125.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَمَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَهْدِيَهُ يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلَامِ وَمَنْ يُرِدْ أَنْ يُضِلَّهُ يَجْعَلْ صَدْرَهُ ضَيِّقًا حَرَجًا كَأَنَّمَا يَصَّعَّدُ فِي السَّمَاءِ كَذَلِكَ يَجْعَلُ اللَّهُ الرِّجْسَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ) (125).
His saying (فَمَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ): it is like (مَنْ يَشَأِ اللَّهُ يُضْلِلْهُ), which has been discussed. (ضَيِّقًا): the second object of «يَجْعَلْ». Whoever doubles the yāʾ makes it an adjective; whoever reads it undoubled (ضَيْقًا), it may be an adjective, like مَيِّت and مَيْت, or a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "possessing narrowness." (حَرَجًا): with kasra on the rāʾ (حَرِجًا) it is an adjective of ضَيِّق, or a third object, just as it is permissible for a mubtadaʾ (subject) to be given several predicates after it, all of them together in the position of a single khabar (predicate), as in «حُلْوٌ حَامِضٌ» ("sweet-sour"); on every analysis it reinforces the meaning. It is also read with fatḥa on the rāʾ (حَرَجًا), as a maṣdar, i.e. "possessing constriction." It has also been said to be the plural of حَرَجَة, like قَصَبَة and قَصَب, the hāʾ in it being for intensification. (كَأَنَّمَا): in the position of the accusative as another khabar, or as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in حَرَج, or in ضَيِّق.
(يَصَّعَّدُ): and يَصَّاعَدُ — with the ṣād doubled in both — i.e. يَتَصَعَّدُ ("ascends with effort"). It is also read «يَصْعَدُ», undoubled.

ukberi-tibyan:126-126.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَهَذَا صِرَاطُ رَبِّكَ مُسْتَقِيمًا قَدْ فَصَّلْنَا الْآيَاتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَذَّكَّرُونَ) (126).
His saying (مُسْتَقِيمًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) of صِرَاطُ رَبِّكَ, and what governs it is the [particle of] alerting or the pointing (the demonstrative).

ukberi-tibyan:127-127.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لَهُمْ دَارُ السَّلَامِ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ) (127).
His saying (لَهُمْ دَارُ السَّلَامِ): it may be a resumptive (new) sentence; or in the position of the genitive as an adjective of قَوْم; or accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «يَذَّكَّرُونَ».
(عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ): a ḥāl of دَارُ السَّلَامِ, or an adverbial of the [notion of] being established implied in «لَهُمْ».

ukberi-tibyan:128-128.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعًا يَا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ قَدِ اسْتَكْثَرْتُمْ مِنَ الْإِنْسِ وَقَالَ أَوْلِيَاؤُهُمْ مِنَ الْإِنْسِ رَبَّنَا اسْتَمْتَعَ بَعْضُنَا بِبَعْضٍ وَبَلَغْنَا أَجَلَنَا الَّذِي أَجَّلْتَ لَنَا قَالَ النَّارُ مَثْوَاكُمْ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ حَكِيمٌ عَلِيمٌ) (128).
His saying (وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ): i.e. "and remember the day," or: "and We shall say, on the day He gathers them: «يَا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ»." (مِنَ الْإِنْسِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «أَوْلِيَاؤُهُمْ». It has been read «آجَالَنَا», in the plural, with «الَّذِي» masculine and singular.
Abū ʿAlī said: it is a generic noun, and he put الَّذِي in the place of الَّتِي.
(خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا): a ḥāl, and regarding what governs it there are two views. The first: الْمَثْوَى, on the view that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning الثَّوَاء ("abiding"), the implied form being: "the Fire is the place of your abiding."
The second: what governs it is the meaning of the annexation (iḍāfa), مَثْوَاكُمْ being a place, and a [noun of] place does not govern.
(إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ): it is an exception from a different genus.
It may also be from the same genus, in two ways. The first: that it is an exception from time, which the meaning indicates, because "abiding forever" (الْخُلُود) indicates perpetuity; it is as though He said: "abiding therein at all times except what Allah wills," i.e. except the time of Allah's willing.
The second: that «مَا» means «مَنْ» ("whoever").

ukberi-tibyan:130-130.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِنْكُمْ يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكُمْ آيَاتِي وَيُنْذِرُونَكُمْ لِقَاءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هَذَا قَالُوا شَهِدْنَا عَلَى أَنْفُسِنَا وَغَرَّتْهُمُ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا وَشَهِدُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا كَافِرِينَ) (130).
His saying (يَقُصُّونَ): in the position of the nominative as an adjective of رُسُل. It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «مِنْكُمْ».

ukberi-tibyan:131-131.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ذَلِكَ أَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ رَبُّكَ مُهْلِكَ الْقُرَى بِظُلْمٍ وَأَهْلُهَا غَافِلُونَ) (131).
His saying (ذَلِكَ): it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "the matter is that."
(أَنْ لَمْ): أَنْ is maṣdariyya, or lightened from the heavy form (أَنَّ), and the lām is omitted, i.e. "because (لِأَنْ) your Lord would not …"; its position is accusative, or genitive, according to the disagreement. (بِظُلْمٍ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), or an object attached to (mutaʿalliq) مُهْلِك.

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تَطْرُدِ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَدَاةِ وَالْعَشِيِّ يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُ مَا عَلَيْكَ مِنْ حِسَابِهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ وَمَا مِنْ حِسَابِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَتَطْرُدَهُمْ فَتَكُونَ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ) (٥٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِالْغَدَاةِ): its origin is غَدْوَةٌ; the wāw was changed into an alif because it was vowelled and the letter before it had fatḥa; and it is indefinite. [Translator's note: the change described requires the wāw to be vowelled, i.e. غَدَوَةٌ.] It is also read «بِالْغُدْوَةِ», with ḍamma on the ghayn, sukūn on the dāl and a wāw after it; He made it definite with the alif and lām, though it is mostly used as a definite proper name (ʿalam); here He has made it definite with the alif and lām.
As for (الْعَشِيُّ): it is said that it is singular, and it is said that it is the plural of عَشِيَّة.
And (يُرِيدُونَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). (مِنْ شَيْءٍ): مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida), and its position is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); عَلَيْكَ is the khabar (predicate), and مِنْ حِسَابِهِمْ is a naʿt (adjective) of شَيْءٍ which was put before it and so became a ḥāl. Likewise the one after it, except that He put «مِنْ حِسَابِكَ» before عَلَيْهِمْ. It is also possible that the khabar is مِنْ حِسَابِهِمْ and that عَلَيْكَ is a naʿt of شَيْءٍ placed before it.
(فَتَطْرُدَهُمْ): an answer to the negating مَا; for that reason it is accusative.
(فَتَكُونَ): the answer to the prohibition, which is «لَا تَطْرُدْ».

ukberi-tibyan:53-53.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَذَلِكَ فَتَنَّا بَعْضَهُمْ بِبَعْضٍ لِيَقُولُوا أَهَؤُلَاءِ مَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ بَيْنِنَا أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِأَعْلَمَ بِالشَّاكِرِينَ) (٥٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِيَقُولُوا): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to فَتَنَّا, i.e. "We tested them so that they would say, and then We punish them for their saying". It may also be the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba).
(هَؤُلَاءِ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (مَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ) is the khabar (predicate); and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying. It is also possible that هَؤُلَاءِ is in the position of the accusative by an omitted verb explained by what follows it, its implied form being "has He singled out these?" or "has He favoured…?". And (مِنْ) is attached to مَنَّ, i.e. "He distinguished them above us".
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from عَلَيْهِمْ, i.e. "set apart (from among us)".
(بِالشَّاكِرِينَ): attached to أَعْلَمَ, because it is a ẓarf (adverbial/prepositional phrase), and a ẓarf can be governed by the meaning of the verb, unlike the object; for the afʿal (elative) form does not govern it.

ukberi-tibyan:54-54.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا جَاءَكَ الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِآيَاتِنَا فَقُلْ سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ كَتَبَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ الرَّحْمَةَ أَنَّهُ مَنْ عَمِلَ مِنْكُمْ سُوءًا بِجَهَالَةٍ ثُمَّ تَابَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ وَأَصْلَحَ فَأَنَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) (٥٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِذَا جَاءَكَ): what governs إِذَا is the meaning of the apodosis (jawāb), i.e. "when they come to you, greet them". And (سَلَامٌ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); that is permissible although it is indefinite because of the meaning of the verb in it.
(كَتَبَ رَبُّكُمْ): this clause is also reported speech after the saying.
(أَنَّهُ مَنْ عَمِلَ): it is read with kasra on إِنَّ and with fatḥa. In the kasra there are two views. One of them: it begins anew, the sentence being complete before it.
The second: that He treated «كَتَبَ» like قَالَ, so إِنَّ after it took kasra.
As for the fatḥa, there are two views on it. One of them: it is a badal (substitute) of الرَّحْمَةَ, i.e. "He has prescribed that whoever does…".
The second: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "upon Him is that whoever does…", what precedes it indicating that. The hāʾ is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); and مَنْ means الَّذِي (the one who) or is conditional, and its position is that of a mubtadaʾ.
And (مِنْكُمْ) is in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun.
And (بِجَهَالَةٍ) is also a ḥāl, i.e. "being ignorant".
It may also be a mafʿūl bihi (object), i.e. "because of ignorance". [Translator's note: so in the text; the gloss "because of" would more naturally make it a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose/cause) or an adverbial of cause.]
The hāʾ in «بَعْدِهِ» refers to the deed or to the evil.
(فَإِنَّهُ): it is read with kasra; it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the first أَنَّ, or, according to some, a repetition of the first. On this view the khabar of «مَنْ» is omitted, the context indicating it. It is also possible that the referring pronoun is omitted, i.e. "then He is forgiving to him". If you make «مَنْ» conditional, the matter is the same.
It is also read with fatḥa; it is then a repetition of the first on the reading of those who read the first with fatḥa, or a badal of it according to some. Both are weak, for two reasons. One of them: a badal is not accompanied by a particle with meaning, unless you make the fāʾ redundant (zāʾida), and that is weak.
The second: that this leads to «مَنْ» being left with no khabar, and with no apodosis if you make it conditional.
The right view is that «أَنَّ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "then his case is that He is forgiving to him"; or that the omitted element is a ẓarf, i.e. "upon Him is that He…", so that أَنَّ is either a mubtadaʾ or a fāʿil (agent).

ukberi-tibyan:55-55.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَذَلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ الْآيَاتِ وَلِتَسْتَبِينَ سَبِيلُ الْمُجْرِمِينَ) (٥٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَكَذَلِكَ): the kāf is a description of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "We set out the signs in detail, a setting-out like that".
«وَلِيَسْتَبِينَ»: it is read with yāʾ, with «سَبِيلُ» as fāʿil (agent), i.e. "that it become clear"; He treated السَّبِيل as masculine, which is a dialectal usage for it; and from it is His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِنْ يَرَوْا سَبِيلَ الْغَيِّ يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلًا).
It is also possible that the reading with yāʾ is on the basis that the femininity of السَّبِيل is not real (ghayr ḥaqīqī).
It is read with tāʾ, السَّبِيل being a feminine agent, which is a dialectal usage for it; and from it is (قُلْ هَذِهِ سَبِيلِي).
It is also read with السَّبِيل in the accusative, the agent being the one addressed, and the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, i.e. "so that you may discern (the way), We have set out (the signs)".

ukberi-tibyan:57-57.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ إِنِّي عَلَى بَيِّنَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّي وَكَذَّبْتُمْ بِهِ مَا عِنْدِي مَا تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ بِهِ إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ يَقُصُّ الْحَقَّ وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الْفَاصِلِينَ) (٥٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَكَذَّبْتُمْ): it may be resumptive (beginning anew), or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), with قَدْ intended along with it. The hāʾ in «بِهِ» refers to رَبِّي.
It may also refer to the sense of الْبَيِّنَة, because it has the meaning of "the proof" and "the evidence".
(يَقْضِي الْحَقَّ): it is read with ḍād, from al-qaḍāʾ (judging), and with ṣād, from al-qaṣaṣ (narrating); the first suits the ending of the verse better.

ukberi-tibyan:59-59.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَعِنْدَهُ مَفَاتِحُ الْغَيْبِ لَا يَعْلَمُهَا إِلَّا هُوَ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ وَمَا تَسْقُطُ مِنْ وَرَقَةٍ إِلَّا يَعْلَمُهَا وَلَا حَبَّةٍ فِي ظُلُمَاتِ الْأَرْضِ وَلَا رَطْبٍ وَلَا يَابِسٍ إِلَّا فِي كِتَابٍ مُبِينٍ) (٥٩)
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَفَاتِحُ): it is the plural of مَفْتَح, and الْمَفْتَح is "the storehouse". As for that with which one opens, it is مِفْتَاح, and its plural is مَفَاتِيح; and مِفْتَح has also been said (for it).
(لَا يَعْلَمُهَا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from مَفَاتِحُ; what governs it is what the ẓarf is attached to, or the ẓarf itself, if مَفَاتِحُ is made nominative by it. And (مِنْ وَرَقَةٍ) is the fāʿil (agent). (وَلَا حَبَّةٍ): maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the wording of وَرَقَةٍ; if it were made nominative according to the position, it would be permissible.
(وَلَا رَطْبٍ وَلَا يَابِسٍ): the same; and it has been read in the nominative according to the position.
(إِلَّا فِي كِتَابٍ): i.e. "except that it is in a Book". It is not permissible for it to be an exception governed by «يَعْلَمُهَا», because the meaning would become "and no leaf falls but He knows it, except in a Book", and its meaning would be turned to affirmation, i.e. "He does not know it in a Book"; and when it is only in a Book, it is necessary that He know it in the Book. So then the second exception is a badal (substitute) of the first, i.e. "and no leaf falls but it is in a Book, and He knows it". [Translator's note: the final words are printed «وَمَا يَعْلَمُهَا», which literally reads "and He does not know it"; this is evidently a misprint, the sense of the argument requiring "and He knows it".]

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَتَوَفَّاكُمْ بِاللَّيْلِ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا جَرَحْتُمْ بِالنَّهَارِ ثُمَّ يَبْعَثُكُمْ فِيهِ لِيُقْضَى أَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) (٦٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِاللَّيْلِ): the bāʾ here means فِي ("in"). That is permissible because the bāʾ is for adhesion (ilṣāq), and what adheres to a time or a place is located in them.
(لِيُقْضَى أَجَلٌ): passive (with the agent unnamed); and it is read with the agent named, with أَجَلًا in the accusative.

ukberi-tibyan:61-61.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَهُوَ الْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ وَيُرْسِلُ عَلَيْكُمْ حَفَظَةً حَتَّى إِذَا جَاءَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ تَوَفَّتْهُ رُسُلُنَا وَهُمْ لَا يُفَرِّطُونَ) (٦١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَيُرْسِلُ عَلَيْكُمْ): it admits four views. First: that it is resumptive. Second: that it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to His saying «يَتَوَفَّاكُمْ» and the imperfect verbs after it.
Third: that it is conjoined to الْقَاهِرُ, because the active participle has the meaning of "he does"; and it is like their saying الطَّائِرُ الذُّبَابُ فَيَغْضَبُ زَيْدٌ ("the fly is the one that flies, and Zayd gets angry"). [Translator's note: the usual form of this grammarians' example is «الطَّائِرُ فَيَغْضَبُ زَيْدٌ الذُّبَابُ» ("the one that flies, so that Zayd gets angry, is the fly"); the text's word order is translated as printed.] Fourth: that the implied form is "and He sends", the clause being a ḥāl (circumstantial), either from the pronoun in الْقَاهِرُ or from the pronoun in the ẓarf. On عَلَيْكُمْ there are two views. One of them: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يُرْسِلُ. The second: that it is intended to come later, and in this there are two views. One of them: that it is attached to «حَفَظَةً» itself, with the object omitted, i.e. "He sends those who keep record of your deeds against you".
The second: that it is a naʿt (adjective) of حَفَظَةً put before it, so it became a ḥāl.
(تَوَفَّتْهُ): it is read with tāʾ, treating the group as feminine, and with an alif pronounced with imāla, intending the plural.
And it is read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, «تَتَوَفَّاهُ», as an imperfect. (يُفَرِّطُونَ): with shadda, i.e. "they fall short of what they were commanded".
And it is read, irregularly, without shadda, i.e. "they exceed what they were commanded".

ukberi-tibyan:62-62.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ رُدُّوا إِلَى اللَّهِ مَوْلَاهُمُ الْحَقِّ أَلَا لَهُ الْحُكْمُ وَهُوَ أَسْرَعُ الْحَاسِبِينَ) (٦٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ثُمَّ رُدُّوا): the majority read with ḍamma on the rāʾ, the kasra of the first dāl being dropped so that assimilation (idghām) is possible. It is also read with kasra on the rāʾ, by transferring the kasra of the first dāl to the rāʾ.
(مَوْلَاهُمُ الْحَقِّ): two adjectives (ṣifa). And الْحَقَّ has been read in the accusative as the adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "the true returning", or by an implied أَعْنِي ("I mean").

ukberi-tibyan:63-63.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ مَنْ يُنَجِّيكُمْ مِنْ ظُلُمَاتِ الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ تَدْعُونَهُ تَضَرُّعًا وَخُفْيَةً لَئِنْ أَنْجَانَا مِنْ هَذِهِ لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الشَّاكِرِينَ) (٦٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُنَجِّيكُمْ): it is read with shadda and without it; the past is أَنْجَا and نَجَّى, and the hamza and the shadda are for making the verb transitive. [Translator's note: the usual spelling is أَنْجَى.]
(تَدْعُونَهُ): in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object pronoun in «يُنَجِّيكُمْ».
(تَضَرُّعًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun), governed by تَدْعُونَ, not through its wording but through its meaning.
It may also be a maṣdar in the position of the ḥāl; and likewise «خُفْيَةً».
It is read with ḍamma on the khāʾ and with kasra, and they are two dialectal forms.
It has also been read «وَخِيفَةً», from al-khawf (fear); it is like His saying, Exalted is He: (وَاذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ فِي نَفْسِكَ تَضَرُّعًا وَخِيفَةً). (لَئِنْ أَنْجَيْتَنَا): in the second person, i.e. "saying: if You deliver us".
And it is read (لَئِنْ أَنْجَانَا) in the third person, which agrees with His saying يَدْعُونَهُ. [Translator's note: the verse as quoted reads تَدْعُونَهُ; the third-person form refers to the reading يَدْعُونَهُ or to the reported speech.]
(مِنْ هَذِهِ): i.e. "from this darkness and distress".

ukberi-tibyan:65-65.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ هُوَ الْقَادِرُ عَلَى أَنْ يَبْعَثَ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابًا مِنْ فَوْقِكُمْ أَوْ مِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِكُمْ أَوْ يَلْبِسَكُمْ شِيَعًا وَيُذِيقَ بَعْضَكُمْ بَأْسَ بَعْضٍ انْظُرْ كَيْفَ نُصَرِّفُ الْآيَاتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَفْقَهُونَ) (٦٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ فَوْقِكُمْ): it may be a description of الْعَذَاب, or it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to يَبْعَثَ; and likewise (مِنْ تَحْتِ). (أَوْ يَلْبِسَكُمْ): the majority read with fatḥa on the yāʾ, i.e. "confuse for you your affairs"; the preposition and the object were omitted. The better view is that the implied form is "confuse your affairs", the muḍāf being omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place.
It is also read with ḍamma on the yāʾ, i.e. "cover you all with discord".
And (شِيَعًا) is the plural of شِيعَة, and it is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
It is also said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), governed by «يَلْبِسَكُمْ» though not of its wording.
It may also, on this view, be a ḥāl, i.e. "differing (among yourselves)".

ukberi-tibyan:66-66.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَذَّبَ بِهِ قَوْمُكَ وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ قُلْ لَسْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ بِوَكِيلٍ) (٦٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَسْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ): عَلَى is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «وَكِيلٍ».
On this basis it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «وَكِيلٍ», according to the view of those who permit placing the ḥāl before the preposition.

ukberi-tibyan:67-67.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِكُلِّ نَبَإٍ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ) (٦٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مُسْتَقَرٌّ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being the ẓarf before it; or a fāʿil (agent) governed by the ẓarf. It is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning "settling"; it may also mean the place (of settling).

ukberi-tibyan:68-68.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ الَّذِينَ يَخُوضُونَ فِي آيَاتِنَا فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ حَتَّى يَخُوضُوا فِي حَدِيثٍ غَيْرِهِ وَإِمَّا يُنْسِيَنَّكَ الشَّيْطَانُ فَلَا تَقْعُدْ بَعْدَ الذِّكْرَى مَعَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ) (٦٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (غَيْرِهِ): He made the hāʾ masculine only because He referred it to the sense of الْآيَات, since they are discourse and Quran.
(يُنْسِيَنَّكَ): it is read without shadda and with shadda; its past is نَسِيَ and أَنْسَى, and the hamza and the shadda are for making the verb transitive to the second object, which is omitted, i.e. "makes you forget the remembrance" or "the truth". [Translator's note: for the reading with shadda the past would be نَسَّى; the text gives نَسِيَ.]

ukberi-tibyan:69-69.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا عَلَى الَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ مِنْ حِسَابِهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ وَلَكِنْ ذِكْرَى لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ) (٦٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ شَيْءٍ): مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida), and مِنْ حِسَابِهِمْ is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the implied sense is "anything of their reckoning". (وَلَكِنْ ذِكْرَى): i.e. "but We remind them a reminding", so it is in the position of the accusative. It may also be in the position of the nominative, i.e. "this is a reminder" or "upon them is a reminder".

ukberi-tibyan:70-70.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَذَرِ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا دِينَهُمْ لَعِبًا وَلَهْوًا وَغَرَّتْهُمُ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا وَذَكِّرْ بِهِ أَنْ تُبْسَلَ نَفْسٌ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ لَيْسَ لَهَا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَلِيٌّ وَلَا شَفِيعٌ وَإِنْ تَعْدِلْ كُلَّ عَدْلٍ لَا يُؤْخَذْ مِنْهَا أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ أُبْسِلُوا بِمَا كَسَبُوا لَهُمْ شَرَابٌ مِنْ حَمِيمٍ وَعَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ) (٧٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ تُبْسَلَ): a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. "for fear that (a soul) be given up to destruction". (لَيْسَ لَهَا): the clause may be in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of نَفْسٌ, or in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in كَسَبَتْ, or it may be resumptive. (مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ): in the position of the ḥāl, i.e. "it has no protector apart from Allah".
It is also possible that «مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ» is the khabar (predicate) of لَيْسَ, with لَهَا as a clarification (tabyīn); and we have mentioned an example of it.
(كُلَّ عَدْلٍ): «كُلَّ» is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because it takes the status of what it is put in construct with.
(أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ): plural according to the meaning. أُولَئِكَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and on the khabar there are two views. One of them: الَّذِينَ أُبْسِلُوا. On this view, His saying (لَهُمْ شَرَابٌ) has two views. One of them: it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in أُبْسِلُوا. The second: it is resumptive.
The other view: that the khabar is لَهُمْ شَرَابٌ, and الَّذِينَ أُبْسِلُوا is a badal (substitute) of أُولَئِكَ or a naʿt; or it is also a khabar, with لَهُمْ شَرَابٌ a second khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:132-132.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلِكُلٍّ دَرَجَاتٌ مِمَّا عَمِلُوا وَمَا رَبُّكَ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ) (132).
His saying (وَلِكُلٍّ): i.e. "and for every one." (مِمَّا): in the position of the nominative as an adjective of دَرَجَات.

ukberi-tibyan:133-133.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَرَبُّكَ الْغَنِيُّ ذُو الرَّحْمَةِ إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ وَيَسْتَخْلِفْ مِنْ بَعْدِكُمْ مَا يَشَاءُ كَمَا أَنْشَأَكُمْ مِنْ ذُرِّيَّةِ قَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ) (133).
His saying (كَمَا أَنْشَأَكُمْ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a succession like …"
(مِنْ ذُرِّيَّةِ): for the beginning of the extent. It has also been said that it has the sense of substitution, i.e. "just as He produced you in place of the offspring of «قَوْمٍ» (another people)."

ukberi-tibyan:134-134.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ مَا تُوعَدُونَ لَآتٍ وَمَا أَنْتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ) (134).
His saying (إِنَّ مَا تُوعَدُونَ): مَا means «الَّذِي» ("that which"), and «لَآتٍ» is the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ. It is not permissible for «مَا» here to be the restraining mā (kāffa), because His saying لَآتٍ prevents that.

ukberi-tibyan:135-135.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ يَا قَوْمِ اعْمَلُوا عَلَى مَكَانَتِكُمْ إِنِّي عَامِلٌ فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ تَكُونُ لَهُ عَاقِبَةُ الدَّارِ إِنَّهُ لَا يُفْلِحُ الظَّالِمُونَ) (135).
His saying (مَنْ تَكُونُ): «مَنْ» may mean «الَّذِي» ("the one who"), or be interrogative, like His saying «أَعْلَمُ مَنْ يَضِلُّ».

ukberi-tibyan:136-136.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ مِمَّا ذَرَأَ مِنَ الْحَرْثِ وَالْأَنْعَامِ نَصِيبًا فَقَالُوا هَذَا لِلَّهِ بِزَعْمِهِمْ وَهَذَا لِشُرَكَائِنَا فَمَا كَانَ لِشُرَكَائِهِمْ فَلَا يَصِلُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَمَا كَانَ لِلَّهِ فَهُوَ يَصِلُ إِلَى شُرَكَائِهِمْ سَاءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ) (136).
His saying (مِمَّا ذَرَأَ): it may be attached to (mutaʿalliq) جَعَلَ, or be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of نَصِيب.
(مِنَ الْحَرْثِ): it may be attached to ذَرَأَ, or be a ḥāl of «مَا» or of the omitted returning pronoun.

ukberi-tibyan:137-137.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَكَذَلِكَ زَيَّنَ لِكَثِيرٍ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ قَتْلَ أَوْلَادِهِمْ شُرَكَاؤُهُمْ لِيُرْدُوهُمْ وَلِيَلْبِسُوا عَلَيْهِمْ دِينَهُمْ وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ مَا فَعَلُوهُ فَذَرْهُمْ وَمَا يَفْتَرُونَ) (137).
His saying (وَكَذَلِكَ زَيَّنَ): it is read with fatḥa on the zāy and the yāʾ, naming the agent, which is شُرَكَاؤُهُمْ; the object is «قَتْلَ», and it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its object.
It is also read with ḍamma on the zāy and kasra on the yāʾ (زُيِّنَ), as a passive verb (whose agent is not named), with «قَتْلُ» in the nominative as standing in the place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent), «أَوْلَادَهُمْ» in the accusative as the object of the killing, and «شُرَكَائِهِمْ» in the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); the two [the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi] have been separated by the object. This is far-fetched, and it occurs only under the necessity of poetry.
It is also read in the same way except with أَوْلَادِهِمْ in the genitive by annexation, and «شُرَكَائِهِمْ» also in the genitive as a badal (substitute) of the أَوْلَاد, because their children are their partners in their religion, their livelihood and other things.
It is also read in the same way except with الشُّرَكَاء in the nominative (شُرَكَاؤُهُمْ). On this there are two views. The first: that it is nominative by an omitted verb, as though it were said: "Who made it seem fair?" and He said: "Their partners," i.e. "their partners made it seem fair." In all of this, the killing is annexed to its object.
The second: that شُرَكَاؤُهُمْ is nominative by the killing (as its agent), because the partners stir up killing among them before it, and it is possible that the killing actually takes place from them. (وَلِيَلْبِسُوا): with kasra on the bāʾ, from لَبَسْتُ الْأَمْرَ — with fatḥa on the bāʾ in the past — when I make a matter obscure.
In the irregular (shādhdh) readings it is read with fatḥa on the bāʾ (وَلِيَلْبَسُوا); it has been said that this is a dialectal variant, and it has also been said that He made the religion to them like clothing upon them.

ukberi-tibyan:138-138.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقَالُوا هَذِهِ أَنْعَامٌ وَحَرْثٌ حِجْرٌ لَا يَطْعَمُهَا إِلَّا مَنْ نَشَاءُ بِزَعْمِهِمْ وَأَنْعَامٌ حُرِّمَتْ ظُهُورُهَا وَأَنْعَامٌ لَا يَذْكُرُونَ اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا افْتِرَاءً عَلَيْهِ سَيَجْزِيهِمْ بِمَا كَانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ) (138).
His saying (لَا يَطْعَمُهَا): in the position of the nominative, like what precedes it.
The majority read «حِجْرٌ» with kasra on the ḥāʾ and sukūn on the jīm. It is also read with ḍamma on both (حُجُرٌ), and with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and sukūn on the jīm (حُجْرٌ); its meaning is "forbidden," and the readings are dialectal variants of it.
It is also read «حِرْجٌ», with kasra on the ḥāʾ and the rāʾ placed before the jīm. Its origin is حَرِجٌ, with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and kasra on the rāʾ, but it was lightened and [the vowel] transferred, as with فَخْذ and فَخِذ.
It has also been said to be a case of metathesis (maqlūb), like عَمِيق and مَعِيق. (بِزَعْمِهِمْ): attached to (mutaʿalliq) قَالُوا; fatḥa, kasra and ḍamma on the zāy are all permissible, and they are dialectal variants.
(افْتِرَاءً): accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because their reported saying has the meaning of "they fabricated."
It has also been said to be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). If you make it accusative as a maṣdar, His saying «عَلَيْهِ» is attached to قَالُوا, not to the maṣdar itself; and if you make it a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, you attach it to the maṣdar itself. It may also be attached to an omitted word, as an adjective of افْتِرَاء.

ukberi-tibyan:139-139.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقَالُوا مَا فِي بُطُونِ هَذِهِ الْأَنْعَامِ خَالِصَةٌ لِذُكُورِنَا وَمُحَرَّمٌ عَلَى أَزْوَاجِنَا وَإِنْ يَكُنْ مَيْتَةً فَهُمْ فِيهِ شُرَكَاءُ سَيَجْزِيهِمْ وَصْفَهُمْ إِنَّهُ حَكِيمٌ عَلِيمٌ) (139).
His saying (مَا فِي بُطُونِ): «مَا» means «الَّذِي» ("that which"), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and (خَالِصَةً) is its khabar (predicate); it was made feminine according to the meaning, because what is in the bellies is livestock. «[Translator's note: the source quotes the word here as خَالِصَةً with an accusative ending while calling it the khabar; the verse text above has خَالِصَةٌ.]»
It has also been said that the feminine ending is for intensification, as in عَلَّامَة ("very learned") and نَسَّابَة ("great genealogist").
(لِذُكُورِنَا): attached to (mutaʿalliq) خَالِصَة, or to an omitted word as an adjective of خَالِصَة.
(وَمُحَرَّمٌ): it comes in the masculine, following the wording of «مَا». It is read «خَالِصٌ», without the tāʾ, according to the base form. It is also read «خَالِصَةً», feminine and accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); what governs it is the sense of being established in مَا فِي بُطُونِهَا, and the khabar is لِذُكُورِنَا, which does not govern the ḥāl because it is not inflectable. Al-Akhfash permitted it.
It is also read «خَالِصَةٌ» in the nominative and annexed to the pronoun hāʾ (خَالِصَتُهُ); it is a mubtadaʾ, لِلذُّكُورِ is its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of «مَا». (يَكُنْ مَيْتَةً): it is read with tāʾ (تَكُنْ) and «مَيْتَةً» in the accusative, i.e. "if the livestock is dead."
It is also read with yāʾ (يَكُنْ), following the wording of «مَا». It is also read with tāʾ and «مَيْتَةٌ» in the nominative, on the view that «كَانَ» is the complete (tāmma) one.
(فَهُمْ فِيهِ): the pronoun is masculine, following «مَا».

ukberi-tibyan:140-140.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَدْ خَسِرَ الَّذِينَ قَتَلُوا أَوْلَادَهُمْ سَفَهًا بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ وَحَرَّمُوا مَا رَزَقَهُمُ اللَّهُ افْتِرَاءً عَلَى اللَّهِ قَدْ ضَلُّوا وَمَا كَانُوا مُهْتَدِينَ) (140).
His saying (قَتَلُوا أَوْلَادَهُمْ): it is read undoubled, and doubled (قَتَّلُوا) for multiplicity.
(سَفَهًا): a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or accusative as the maṣdar (verbal noun) of an omitted verb indicated by the speech. (بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). (افْتِرَاءً): like the first one.

ukberi-tibyan:141-141.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَنْشَأَ جَنَّاتٍ مَعْرُوشَاتٍ وَغَيْرَ مَعْرُوشَاتٍ وَالنَّخْلَ وَالزَّرْعَ مُخْتَلِفًا أُكُلُهُ وَالزَّيْتُونَ وَالرُّمَّانَ مُتَشَابِهًا وَغَيْرَ مُتَشَابِهٍ كُلُوا مِنْ ثَمَرِهِ إِذَا أَثْمَرَ وَآتُوا حَقَّهُ يَوْمَ حَصَادِهِ وَلَا تُسْرِفُوا إِنَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْرِفِينَ) (141).
His saying (مُخْتَلِفًا أُكُلُهُ): مُخْتَلِفًا is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara, circumstantial of what will be), because at the time the date palm and the crops come forth there is no produce in them that could be differing or alike. It is like their saying: مَرَرْتُ بِرَجُلٍ مَعَهُ صَقْرٌ صَائِدًا بِهِ غَدًا ("I passed by a man with a falcon, [intending to be] hunting with it tomorrow").
It is also possible that there is an omitted muḍāf in the speech, its implied form being: "the fruit of the date palm and the grain of the crops"; on this view the ḥāl is concurrent (muqārina). (مُتَشَابِهًا): also a ḥāl. (حَصَادِهِ): it is read with fatḥa and with kasra (حِصَادِهِ), and they are two dialectal variants.

ukberi-tibyan:142-142.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمِنَ الْأَنْعَامِ حَمُولَةً وَفَرْشًا كُلُوا مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ) (142).
His saying (حَمُولَةً وَفَرْشًا): it is conjoined to جَنَّات, i.e. "and He produced of the livestock some for burden."

ukberi-tibyan:143-143.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ثَمَانِيَةَ أَزْوَاجٍ مِنَ الضَّأْنِ اثْنَيْنِ وَمِنَ الْمَعْزِ اثْنَيْنِ قُلْ آلذَّكَرَيْنِ حَرَّمَ أَمِ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ أَمَّا اشْتَمَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ أَرْحَامُ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ نَبِّئُونِي بِعِلْمٍ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ) (143).
His saying (ثَمَانِيَةَ أَزْوَاجٍ): there are five views on its accusative. The first: it is conjoined to جَنَّات, i.e. "and He produced eight pairs," with the verb and the conjunction omitted; this is weak. The second: that its implied form is: "eat eight pairs."
The third: it is accusative by كُلُوا, its implied form being: "eat of what He has provided you, eight pairs," with وَلَا تُسْرِفُوا parenthetical between them. The fourth: it is a badal (substitute) of «حَمُولَةً وَفَرْشًا». The fifth: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), its implied form being: "differing" or "numerous."
(مِنَ الضَّأْنِ): it is read with sukūn on the hamza and with fatḥa (الضَّأَنِ), and they are two dialectal variants. (اثْنَيْنِ): a badal of ثَمَانِيَة, and the rest of the eight have been conjoined to it. (الْمَعْزِ): fatḥa on the ʿayn and sukūn are two dialectal variants, and it has been read with both. (آلذَّكَرَيْنِ): it is accusative by «حَرَّمَ», and likewise «أَمِ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ», i.e. "or has He forbidden the two females?" (أَمَّا اشْتَمَلَتْ): i.e. "or has He forbidden what … contain?"

ukberi-tibyan:144-144.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمِنَ الْإِبِلِ اثْنَيْنِ وَمِنَ الْبَقَرِ اثْنَيْنِ قُلْ آلذَّكَرَيْنِ حَرَّمَ أَمِ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ أَمَّا اشْتَمَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ أَرْحَامُ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ أَمْ كُنْتُمْ شُهَدَاءَ إِذْ وَصَّاكُمُ اللَّهُ بِهَذَا فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا لِيُضِلَّ النَّاسَ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ) (144).
His saying (أَمْ كُنْتُمْ شُهَدَاءَ): أَمْ is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), i.e. "nay, were you …?"
(إِذْ): governed by «شُهَدَاءَ».

ukberi-tibyan:145-145.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ لَا أَجِدُ فِي مَا أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ مُحَرَّمًا عَلَى طَاعِمٍ يَطْعَمُهُ إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ مَيْتَةً أَوْ دَمًا مَسْفُوحًا أَوْ لَحْمَ خِنْزِيرٍ فَإِنَّهُ رِجْسٌ أَوْ فِسْقًا أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ بَاغٍ وَلَا عَادٍ فَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) (145).
His saying (يَطْعَمُهُ): in the position of the genitive as an adjective of طَاعِم. It is also read «يَطَّعِمُهُ», with doubling and kasra on the ʿayn; the original is يَتَطَعَّمُهُ, then the tāʾ was changed into ṭāʾ and the first was assimilated into it.
(إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ): an exception from the same genus, and its position is accusative, i.e. "I do not find anything forbidden except carrion." يَكُونُ is read with yāʾ and (مَيْتَةً) in the accusative, i.e. "unless what is eaten is carrion," or "that" …
It is also read with tāʾ (تَكُونَ): "unless the thing eaten (feminine) is carrion."
It is also read with مَيْتَةٌ in the nominative, on the view that «تَكُونَ» is complete (tāmma); but this is weak, because what is conjoined to it is accusative.
(أَوْ فِسْقًا): conjoined to لَحْمَ الْخِنْزِيرِ.
It has also been said that it is conjoined to the position of إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ, the two having been separated by His saying فَإِنَّهُ رِجْسٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:146-146.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ هَادُوا حَرَّمْنَا كُلَّ ذِي ظُفُرٍ وَمِنَ الْبَقَرِ وَالْغَنَمِ حَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ شُحُومَهُمَا إِلَّا مَا حَمَلَتْ ظُهُورُهُمَا أَوِ الْحَوَايَا أَوْ مَا اخْتَلَطَ بِعَظْمٍ ذَلِكَ جَزَيْنَاهُمْ بِبَغْيِهِمْ وَإِنَّا لَصَادِقُونَ) (146).
His saying (كُلَّ ذِي ظُفُرٍ): the majority read it with ḍamma on the ẓāʾ and the fāʾ; it is also read with the fāʾ quiescent (ظُفْرٍ), and with kasra on the ẓāʾ and the quiescent fāʾ (ظِفْرٍ). (وَمِنَ الْبَقَرِ): conjoined to «كُلَّ», and (حَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ شُحُومَهُمَا) was made an explanation of what is forbidden of the cattle.
It is also possible that «مِنَ الْبَقَرِ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second حَرَّمْنَا.
(إِلَّا مَا حَمَلَتْ): in the position of the accusative as an exception from the fats.
(أَوِ الْحَوَايَا): in the position of the accusative, conjoined to «مَا».
It has also been said that it is conjoined to the fats, so that they are also forbidden. The singular of الْحَوَايَا ("entrails") is حَوِيَّة, or حَاوِيَة, or حَاوِيَاء. «أَوْ» here has the meaning of the wāw, or is for detailing their [various] positions, because of the difference of their locations; we have mentioned this at His saying (كُونُوا هُودًا أَوْ نَصَارَى).
(ذَلِكَ): in the position of the accusative by «جَزَيْنَاهُمْ». It has also been said: a mubtadaʾ (subject), the implied form being "We recompensed them with it (جَزَيْنَاهُمُوهُ)." It has also been said to be the khabar (predicate) of an omitted [mubtadaʾ], i.e. "the matter is that."

ukberi-tibyan:147-147.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَإِنْ كَذَّبُوكَ فَقُلْ رَبُّكُمْ ذُو رَحْمَةٍ وَاسِعَةٍ وَلَا يُرَدُّ بَأْسُهُ عَنِ الْقَوْمِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ) (147).
His saying (فَإِنْ كَذَّبُوكَ): a condition, and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is «فَقُلْ رَبُّكُمْ ذُو رَحْمَةٍ»; the implied form is: "then say: He pardons you by deferring the punishment."

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَجَعَلَ الظُّلُمَاتِ وَالنُّورَ ثُمَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ يَعْدِلُونَ) (١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِرَبِّهِمْ): the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَعْدِلُونَ», i.e. "those who disbelieve make others equal to their Lord"; الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا is a mubtadaʾ (subject), يَعْدِلُونَ is the khabar (predicate), and the object is omitted.
On this view the bāʾ may also have the meaning of عَنْ, so there is no omitted object in the speech; rather يَعْدِلُونَ is intransitive, i.e. "they turn away from Him to others".
And the bāʾ may be attached to كَفَرُوا, so the meaning is "those who deny their Lord are deviating from guidance".

ukberi-tibyan:148-148.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (سَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا لَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ مَا أَشْرَكْنَا وَلَا آبَاؤُنَا وَلَا حَرَّمْنَا مِنْ شَيْءٍ كَذَلِكَ كَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ حَتَّى ذَاقُوا بَأْسَنَا قُلْ هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ مِنْ عِلْمٍ فَتُخْرِجُوهُ لَنَا إِنْ تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَإِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا تَخْرُصُونَ) (148).
His saying (وَلَا آبَاؤُنَا): conjoined to the pronoun in أَشْرَكْنَا, and the addition of «لَا» made the emphasis (tawkīd) of the pronoun unnecessary. It has also been said that this does not suffice, because the emphasizing [word] must come before the conjunction, not after the conjunction. (مِنْ شَيْءٍ): مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida).

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ طِينٍ ثُمَّ قَضَى أَجَلًا وَأَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى عِنْدَهُ ثُمَّ أَنْتُمْ تَمْتَرُونَ) (٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ طِينٍ): there is an omitted muḍāf in the speech, i.e. "He created your origin". مِنْ طِينٍ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to خَلَقَ, and مِنْ here marks the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya).
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "He created your origin, being from clay".
(وَأَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى): a qualified mubtadaʾ (subject), and (عِنْدَهُ) is the khabar (predicate).

ukberi-tibyan:150-150.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ هَلُمَّ شُهَدَاءَكُمُ الَّذِينَ يَشْهَدُونَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ حَرَّمَ هَذَا فَإِنْ شَهِدُوا فَلَا تَشْهَدْ مَعَهُمْ وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْوَاءَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا وَالَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ وَهُمْ بِرَبِّهِمْ يَعْدِلُونَ) (150).
His saying (قُلْ هَلُمَّ): the Arabs have two usages for it. One: it has a single form for the singular, dual and plural, masculine and feminine; on this usage it is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl, noun standing for a verb), made indeclinable (mabnī) because it occurs in the place of the indeclinable imperative; its meaning is "bring your witnesses."
The second usage: it varies, so you say هَلُمَّا, هَلُمُّوا, هَلُمِّي and هَلْمُمْنَ; on this usage it is a verb. They disagreed about its origin. The Basrans said: its origin is هَا الْمُمْ, i.e. "make for (it)"; the mīm was assimilated into the mīm and the lām was given a vowel, so the connecting hamza was no longer needed, leaving لُمَّ; then the alif of «هَا», which is for alerting, was dropped, because the lām in لُمَّ is treated as quiescent, its vowel being incidental. The particle of alerting was attached to the imperative form just as it is attached to other forms.
As for the fatḥa on the mīm, there are two views on it. The first: that it was given that vowel because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and neither ḍamma nor kasra was allowed, as they are allowed in رُدَّ, رُدُّ and رُدِّ, because of the length of the word through joining «هَا» to it, and because it is used only with it. The second: that it was given fatḥa because of the compounding, just as خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ ("fifteen") and its class were given fatḥa.
Al-Farrāʾ said: its origin is هَلْ أُمَّ; the vowel of the hamza was cast onto the lām and [the hamza] was dropped. This is far-fetched, because its form is an imperative; and «هَلْ», if it is interrogative, has no meaning entering upon an imperative; if it has the meaning of قَدْ, it does not enter upon an imperative; and if «هَلْ» is a noun of chiding (for driving animals), that one is indeclinable on fatḥa, and besides it has no meaning here.

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَهُوَ اللَّهُ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَفِي الْأَرْضِ يَعْلَمُ سِرَّكُمْ وَجَهْرَكُمْ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا تَكْسِبُونَ) (٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَهُوَ اللَّهُ): هُوَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and اللَّهُ is the khabar (predicate). And on (فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ) there are two views.
First: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَعْلَمُ», i.e. "He knows your secret and your open (deeds) in the heavens and the earth", so they are two adverbials for the knowing. On this view يَعْلَمُ is a second khabar; and اللَّهُ may be a badal (substitute) for هُوَ, with يَعْلَمُ as the khabar.
Second: that «فِي» is attached to the name of Allah, because it has the meaning of "the One worshipped", i.e. "and He is the One worshipped in the heavens and the earth"; on this view يَعْلَمُ is a second khabar, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in "the One worshipped", or resumptive. Abū ʿAlī said: «فِي» may not be attached to the name of Allah, because through the entry of the alif and lām and the change that entered it, it has become like a proper name; and for this reason the Exalted said: (هَلْ تَعْلَمُ لَهُ سَمِيًّا). It is also said: the speech is complete at His saying «فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ», and «فِي الْأَرْضِ» is attached to «يَعْلَمُ»; this is weak, because He, glorified is He, is worshipped in the heavens and in the earth, and knows what is in the heaven and the earth, so neither of the two attributes is restricted to either of the two adverbials.
And (سِرَّكُمْ وَجَهْرَكُمْ): two maṣdars (verbal nouns) with the meaning of passive participles, i.e. "what you keep secret and what you make open"; this is indicated by His saying (وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تُسِرُّونَ وَمَا تُعْلِنُونَ), i.e. "that which…" [Translator's note: the sentence breaks off in the source.] And they may be in their usual sense (as maṣdars).

ukberi-tibyan:151-151.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ تَعَالَوْا أَتْلُ مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ أَلَّا تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئًا وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا أَوْلَادَكُمْ مِنْ إِمْلَاقٍ نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُكُمْ وَإِيَّاهُمْ وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا الْفَوَاحِشَ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَمَا بَطَنَ وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ ذَلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ) (151).
His saying (مَا حَرَّمَ): regarding «مَا» there are two views. The first: it means «الَّذِي» ("that which"), and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "[that which] He forbade (حَرَّمَهُ)."
The second: it is maṣdariyya.
(أَلَّا تُشْرِكُوا): regarding «أَنْ» there are two views.
The first: it means أَيْ ("that is"), so that لَا on this view is a prohibition.
The second: it is maṣdariyya, and regarding its position there are two views:
- The first: it is accusative, and on that there are two views (the first: it is a badal (substitute) of the omitted hāʾ or of «مَا», and «لَا» is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "your Lord has forbidden that you associate partners"; the second: that it is accusative as an incitement (ighrāʾ), what governs it being عَلَيْكُمْ, with the pause on what precedes عَلَى, i.e. "keep to abandoning associating partners").
- The second view: that it is nominative, the implied form being: "what is recited is that you not associate partners," or "what is forbidden is that you associate partners"; «لَا» is redundant on this analysis.
(شَيْئًا): the object of تُشْرِكُوا; we have mentioned it in another place. It is also possible that شَيْئًا is in the position of the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "any association." (وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا): this has been mentioned in al-Baqara. (مِنْ إِمْلَاقٍ): i.e. "because of poverty." (مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَمَا بَطَنَ): two badals of الْفَوَاحِش, a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl); مِنْهَا is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent pronoun. (بِالْحَقِّ): in the position of a ḥāl. (ذَلِكُمْ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ» is the khabar (predicate).
It may also be in the position of the accusative, on the implied form "He has made that binding on you," with وَصَّاكُمْ being an explanation of it.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا تَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ آيَةٍ مِنْ آيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ إِلَّا كَانُوا عَنْهَا مُعْرِضِينَ) (٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ آيَةٍ): its position is nominative, governed by تَأْتِي, and مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida).
And (مِنْ آيَاتِ): in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of آيَةٍ.
And it may be in the position of the nominative, following the position of آيَةٍ.

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوا بِالْحَقِّ لَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِيهِمْ أَنْبَاءُ مَا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ) (٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ): «لَمَّا» is an adverb for كَذَّبُوا, and this (verb) has governed it while being before it; likewise «إِذَا». And (بِهِ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ».

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِنْ قَرْنٍ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَا لَمْ نُمَكِّنْ لَكُمْ وَأَرْسَلْنَا السَّمَاءَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِدْرَارًا وَجَعَلْنَا الْأَنْهَارَ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهِمْ فَأَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَأَنْشَأْنَا مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ قَرْنًا آخَرِينَ) (٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا): كَمْ is an interrogative with the meaning of magnifying (taʿẓīm); for that reason يَرَوْا does not govern it. It is in the position of the accusative governed by أَهْلَكْنَا: كَمْ may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), with «مِنْ قَرْنٍ» a clarification of كَمْ.
And it may be an adverb, with «مِنْ قَرْنٍ» the object of أَهْلَكْنَا and مِنْ redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "how many times have We destroyed generations in them before them".
And كَمْ may be a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "how many times" and "how many destructions"; this recurs often in the Qurʾān. (مَكَّنَّاهُمْ): in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of الْقَرْنِ, and it is made plural according to the meaning.
(مَا لَمْ نُمَكِّنْ لَكُمْ): it has turned from the third person in His saying «أَلَمْ يَرَوْا» to address in لَكُمْ; had He said لَهُمْ it would have been permissible.
And (مَا): an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa), and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. "something which We did not establish for you".
And «مَا» may be maṣdariyya, with the time omitted, i.e. "for the period that We did not establish for you", i.e. the period of their establishment was longer than your period.
And «مَا» may be the object of نُمَكِّنْ according to the meaning, because the meaning is "We gave them what We did not give you".
And (مِدْرَارًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from السَّمَاءَ. And (تَجْرِي): the second object of جَعَلْنَا, or a ḥāl from الْأَنْهَارَ if you make «جَعَلَ» transitive to one object. And (مِنْ تَحْتِهِمْ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to تَجْرِي.
And it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in تَجْرِي, i.e. "while they are beneath them".
And مِنْ تَحْتِهِمْ may be a second object of جَعَلَ, or a ḥāl from الْأَنْهَارَ, with تَجْرِي in the position of a ḥāl from the pronoun in the preposition phrase, i.e. "and We made the rivers beneath them flowing", i.e. "settled, flowing".
