And (مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ): attached to أَنْشَأْنَا; it may not be a ḥāl from قَرْنًا, because it is an adverb of time.

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْ نَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ كِتَابًا فِي قِرْطَاسٍ فَلَمَسُوهُ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ لَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ هَذَا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ) (٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي قِرْطَاسٍ): a naʿt (adjective) of كِتَابًا. It may also be attached (mutaʿalliq) to كِتَابًا, as an adverbial for it. الْكِتَابُ here is what is written on the sheet, not the sheet itself.
الْقِرْطَاسُ with kasra or fatḥa on the qāf are two dialectal forms, and both have been read.
The hāʾ in «لَمَسُوهُ» may refer back to قِرْطَاسٍ, or to كِتَابًا.

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْ جَعَلْنَاهُ مَلَكًا لَجَعَلْنَاهُ رَجُلًا وَلَلَبَسْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ مَا يَلْبِسُونَ) (٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا يَلْبِسُونَ): «مَا» has the meaning of الَّذِي, and it is the object of لَبَسْنَا.

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ فَحَاقَ بِالَّذِينَ سَخِرُوا مِنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ) (١٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ): it is read with kasra on the dāl, according to the basic rule for the meeting of two quiescent letters, and with ḍamma on it, on the view that its vowel was made to follow the vowel of the tāʾ, because the barrier between them is weak. And «مَا» has the meaning of الَّذِي, and it is the fāʿil (agent) of حَاقَ. And (بِهِ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ».
And (مِنْهُمْ): the pronoun is for the messengers, so مِنْهُمْ is attached to سَخِرُوا, in view of His saying فَيَسْخَرُونَ مِنْهُمْ.
In ordinary speech سَخِرْتُ بِهِ ("I mocked him") is also permitted. And the pronoun may refer back to the mockers, so مِنْهُمْ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in سَخِرُوا.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ سِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ ثُمَّ انْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ) (١١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَيْفَ كَانَ): كَيْفَ is the khabar (predicate) of kāna. And (عَاقِبَةُ): its noun. The verb was not made feminine because الْعَاقِبَةُ has the meaning of الْمَعَادُ ("the outcome"), so it is in the sense of the masculine; and because the feminine is not a real (biological) one.

ukberi-tibyan:71-71.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ أَنَدْعُو مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنْفَعُنَا وَلَا يَضُرُّنَا وَنُرَدُّ عَلَى أَعْقَابِنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَانَا اللَّهُ كَالَّذِي اسْتَهْوَتْهُ الشَّيَاطِينُ فِي الْأَرْضِ حَيْرَانَ لَهُ أَصْحَابٌ يَدْعُونَهُ إِلَى الْهُدَى ائْتِنَا قُلْ إِنَّ هُدَى اللَّهِ هُوَ الْهُدَى وَأُمِرْنَا لِنُسْلِمَ لِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ) (٧١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنَدْعُو): the interrogative has the meaning of rebuke (tawbīkh).
And (مَا) means الَّذِي (that which), or is an indefinite noun described by what follows. And (مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to نَدْعُو. It may not be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (يَنْفَعُنَا), nor an object of يَنْفَعُنَا, because it comes before «مَا», and the ṣila (relative clause) and the adjective do not govern what precedes the relative and the described noun. (وَنُرَدُّ): maʿṭūf (conjoined) to نَدْعُو; it may also be a clause in the position of the ḥāl, i.e. "while we are turned back".
And (عَلَى أَعْقَابِنَا) is a ḥāl from the pronoun in نُرَدُّ, i.e. "we are turned back reversing" or "falling behind".
(كَالَّذِي): there are two views on the kāf. One of them: it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in نُرَدُّ, or a badal (substitute) of «عَلَى أَعْقَابِنَا», i.e. "resembling the one whom «اسْتَهْوَتْهُ»". The second: that it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a turning back like the turning back of the one whom (the devils) lured away".
اسْتَهْوَتْهُ is read thus, and also اسْتَهْوَاهُ, like تَوَفَّتْهُ and تَوَفَّاهُ; and it has been mentioned.
And «الَّذِي» may be singular here, i.e. "like the man who…" or "like the party which…".
It may also be generic, the intended meaning being الَّذِينَ. (فِي الْأَرْضِ): it may be attached to اسْتَهْوَتْهُ, or a ḥāl from «حَيْرَانَ», i.e. "bewildered, being in the earth".
It may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun in حَيْرَانَ, or a ḥāl from the hāʾ in اسْتَهْوَتْهُ.
And (حَيْرَانَ) is a ḥāl from the hāʾ, or from the pronoun in the ẓarf; and it is a diptote (not taking tanwīn) because its feminine is حَيْرَى. (لَهُ أَصْحَابٌ): the clause may be resumptive, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in حَيْرَانَ, or from the pronoun in the ẓarf, or a badal of the ḥāl before it.
(ائْتِنَا): i.e. "saying: come to us". (لِنُسْلِمَ): i.e. "we have been commanded that, in order that we submit". It is also said: the lām has the meaning of the bāʾ; and it is said: it is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "that we submit".

ukberi-tibyan:72-72.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَنْ أَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَاتَّقُوهُ وَهُوَ الَّذِي إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ) (٧٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَنْ أَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ): أَنْ is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to لِنُسْلِمَ. It is also said: it is conjoined to His saying (إِنَّ الْهُدَى هُدَى اللَّهِ), the implied sense being "and say: establish…". [Translator's note: the verse (71) reads «إِنَّ هُدَى اللَّهِ هُوَ الْهُدَى»; the text quotes it as given.] And it is said: it is construed according to the meaning, i.e. "it was said to us: submit, and establish…".

ukberi-tibyan:73-73.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ وَيَوْمَ يَقُولُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ قَوْلُهُ الْحَقُّ وَلَهُ الْمُلْكُ يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ) (٧٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَيَوْمَ يَقُولُ): there are a number of views on it:
First: it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the hāʾ in «اتَّقُوهُ», i.e. "and fear the punishment of the day He says".
Second: it is conjoined to السَّمَاوَاتِ, i.e. "He created the day He says".
Third: it is the khabar (predicate) of «قَوْلُهُ الْحَقُّ», i.e. "and His word is the truth on the day He says"; the wāw enters on the clause whose khabar is placed first, and الْحَقُّ is a naʿt (adjective) of قَوْلُهُ.
Fourth: it is an adverbial (ẓarf) of the meaning of the clause قَوْلُهُ الْحَقُّ, i.e. "His word is realised on the day He says: Be".
Fifth: it is accusative on the implied form "and remember". As for the fāʿil (agent) of «فَيَكُونُ», there are several views on it. First: it is everything that Allah creates on the Day of Resurrection.
Second: it is the pronoun of what is blown into, of the forms (al-ṣuwar), indicated by His saying «يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ». [Translator's note: «الصُّوَر» here is the plural of ṣūra, "form", following the view that what is blown into is the forms (bodies).]
Third: it is the pronoun of the day. Fourth: it is قَوْلُهُ الْحَقُّ, i.e. "then His true word comes into being"; on this view قَوْلُهُ means "what He says", i.e. "then that to which He said 'Be' comes into being".
So it results from what we have mentioned that «قَوْلُهُ» may be a fāʿil with «الْحَقُّ» its naʿt; or a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the day as its khabar and «الْحَقُّ» its naʿt; or a mubtadaʾ with «الْحَقُّ» its naʿt and «يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ» its khabar; or a mubtadaʾ with «الْحَقُّ» its khabar.
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ): it may be the khabar of «قَوْلُهُ», as we have mentioned; or an adverbial of الْمُلْك, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it, governed by لَهُ; or an adverbial of تُحْشَرُونَ, or of يَقُولُ, or of His saying «الْحَقُّ», or of His saying «عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ». (عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ): the majority read it in the nominative; it may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or the fāʿil of «يَقُولُ كُنْ», or a naʿt of الَّذِي.
It has also been read in the genitive as a badal (substitute) of رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ, or of the hāʾ in لَهُ.

ukberi-tibyan:74-74.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ آزَرَ أَتَتَّخِذُ أَصْنَامًا آلِهَةً إِنِّي أَرَاكَ وَقَوْمَكَ فِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ) (٧٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ): إِذْ is in the position of the accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "and remember", and it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to أَقِيمُوا. And (آزَرَ) is read with madd; its pattern is «أَفْعَل», and it is a diptote because of foreignness and definiteness, according to those who do not derive it from al-azr or al-wizr. Whoever derives it from one of these says it is Arabic, and makes it a diptote because of definiteness and the verbal pattern. It is read with fatḥa on the rāʾ as a badal (substitute) of أَبِيهِ, and with ḍamma as a vocative.
It has been read, among the irregular (shādhdh) readings, with two hamzas both with fatḥa, tanwīn on the rāʾ and sukūn on the zāy; and al-azr is "make, form", like al-asr. [Translator's note: i.e. the reading أَأَزْرًا.]
It is also read with fatḥa on the first and kasra on the second, and in this there are two views. One of them: that the second hamza is the first radical (fāʾ) of the word and is not a substitute, and its meaning is "a burden" (al-thiql). [Translator's note: the text reads «النَّقْلُ» ("transfer"), probably a misprint for «الثِّقْلُ» ("burden"); translated according to the probable sense.]
The second: it is a substitute for wāw; he said: its origin is وَزَرَ, as they said وِعَاءٌ and إِعَاءٌ, and وِسَادَةٌ and إِسَادَةٌ. [Translator's note: the comparison with وِعَاءٌ and وِسَادَةٌ suggests the form وِزْر is meant.] On these two readings the first hamza is the interrogative with the meaning of denial (inkār), and there is no hamza on تَتَّخِذُ. On its accusative case, on this view, there are two views. One of them: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "is it because of your bewilderment and the crookedness of your religion that you take…?".
The second: it is a naʿt (adjective) of أَصْنَامًا put before it and before what governs it, so it became a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "do you take idols, accursed or crooked…?". And (أَصْنَامًا) is the first object.
And (آلِهَةً) is the second. It is permissible to make the first object indefinite because the clause yields useful information; and that is easier with objects than it is with the mubtadaʾ (subject).

ukberi-tibyan:75-75.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَذَلِكَ نُرِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ مَلَكُوتَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَلِيَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُوقِنِينَ) (٧٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَكَذَلِكَ): there are two views on its position. One of them: it is accusative by an implied "and We showed him", the implied form being: "and just as he saw his father and his people in manifest error, We showed him that", i.e. what he saw as right, by Our acquainting him with it.
It may also be accusative by the «نَرَى» after it, as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), the implied form being: "We show him the dominion of the heavens and the earth, a showing like his seeing of his father's error". [Translator's note: so in the text; the verse reads «نُرِي».]
It is also said: the kāf has the meaning of the lām, i.e. "and for that We show him".
The second view: that the kāf is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "and the matter is like that", i.e. as he saw of their error.
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلِيَكُونَ): i.e. "and so that he might be «مِنَ الْمُوقِنِينَ» We showed him".
It is also said: the implied form is "so that he might draw inference, and so that he might be…".

ukberi-tibyan:76-76.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ اللَّيْلُ رَأَى كَوْكَبًا قَالَ هَذَا رَبِّي فَلَمَّا أَفَلَ قَالَ لَا أُحِبُّ الْآفِلِينَ) (٧٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (رَأَى كَوْكَبًا): it is read with fatḥa on the rāʾ and the hamza and with full (unslanted) pronunciation (tafkhīm), according to the original; and with imāla, because the alif is changed from a yāʾ, as when you say رَأَيْتُ رُؤْيَةً. It is also read with the hamza made "between-between" (bayna bayna), which is a kind of imāla. [Translator's note: the text says «الْهَمْزَتَيْنِ» ("the two hamzas"), though the word has a single hamza; probably intended is the hamza and the alif.]
It is also read with the rāʾ made the same way, in harmony with the hamza. It is also read with kasra on both, and in that there are two views. One of them: that he gave the hamza kasra for imāla, then made the rāʾ follow it.
The second: that the original vowel of the hamza is kasra, as shown by your saying in the imperfect يَرَى, i.e. يَرْأَى; it was given fatḥa only because of the guttural letter, as you say وَسِعَ يَسَعُ; then the first letter in the past was given kasra in harmony with the kasra of the hamza. If the alif meets a vowelless letter, as in رَأَى الشَّمْسَ, it has been read with fatḥa on both according to the original, and with kasra on both as explained above.
And with kasra on the rāʾ and fatḥa on the hamza, because the alif dropped out of the pronunciation on account of the vowelless letter after it, and what is dropped here counts as if present; so the kasra of the rāʾ was a pointer to the original being kasra on the hamza, and its fatḥa was an indication of the dropped alif.
(هَذَا رَبِّي): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), the implied form being "Is this my Lord?". It is also said: it is a statement, i.e. it is not an interrogative.

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا رَأَى الشَّمْسَ بَازِغَةً قَالَ هَذَا رَبِّي هَذَا أَكْبَرُ فَلَمَّا أَفَلَتْ قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ إِنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تُشْرِكُونَ) (٧٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَازِغَةً): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الشَّمْس. He said هَذَا in the masculine of the sun only because he meant "this star", or "this rising one", or "this body", or "this light", or "this thing"; or because the femininity is not real.

ukberi-tibyan:79-79.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنِّي وَجَّهْتُ وَجْهِيَ لِلَّذِي فَطَرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ حَنِيفًا وَمَا أَنَا مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ) (٧٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِلَّذِي فَطَرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ): or "to His worship", or "to His good pleasure".

ukberi-tibyan:80-80.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَحَاجَّهُ قَوْمُهُ قَالَ أَتُحَاجُّونِّي فِي اللَّهِ وَقَدْ هَدَانِي وَلَا أَخَافُ مَا تُشْرِكُونَ بِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ رَبِّي شَيْئًا وَسِعَ رَبِّي كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِلْمًا أَفَلَا تَتَذَكَّرُونَ) (٨٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَتُحَاجُّونِّي): it is read with shadda on the nūn, by assimilating the nūn of the indicative into the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya); the original is تُحَاجُّونَنِي.
It is also read without shadda, by dropping one of the two nūns, and there are two views about which is dropped. One of them: it is the nūn of protection, because it is the added one through which the heaviness arose; and that has occurred in poetry. The second: the dropped one is the nūn of the indicative, because there was need of a nūn with kasra on account of the yāʾ, and the nūn of the indicative does not take kasra; and that has occurred in poetry frequently. The poet said:
كُلٌّ لَهُ نِيَّةٌ فِي بُغْضِ صَاحِبِهِ ... بِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ نَقْلِيكُمْ وَتَقْلُونَا
("Each has an intent to hate his fellow; by the grace of Allah we detest you and you detest us.")
i.e. تَقْلُونَنَا. But the second nūn here is not one of protection; rather it is part of the pronoun, and dropping part of the pronoun is not permissible. And it [the second view] is also weak, because the indicative marker is dropped only by a governing word.
(مَا تُشْرِكُونَ بِهِ): «مَا» means الَّذِي (that which), i.e. "and I do not fear the idol which you associate with Him", i.e. with Allah; so the hāʾ in بِهِ is the pronoun of the name of Allah the Exalted.
It is also possible that the hāʾ refers back to مَا, i.e. "and I do not fear that because of which you commit shirk", and it does not refer to Allah.
It is also possible that «مَا» is an indefinite noun described by what follows, or that it is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun).
(إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ): it may be an exception of the same kind as the first (connected exception), the implied form being "except in the state of my Lord's willing", i.e. "I do not fear them in any state except in this state".
It may also be of other than the first kind (disconnected exception), i.e. "but I fear that He may will for me my fearing what you have associated". [Translator's note: the wording «أَنْ يَشَاءَ بِي خَوْفِي مَا أَشْرَكْتُمْ» is translated as printed; the sense is that He might will that I come to fear what you associate.]
And (شَيْئًا) stands in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "any willing"; it may also be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "unless He wills for me a matter other than what I have said".
And (عِلْمًا) is a tamyīz (specification), and (كُلَّ شَيْءٍ) is the object of وَسِعَ, i.e. "He knew everything".
On this interpretation «عِلْمًا» may also be a maṣdar for the meaning of وَسِعَ, because whatever contains a thing has encompassed it, and one who knows a thing encompasses it with his knowledge.

ukberi-tibyan:81-81.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَيْفَ أَخَافُ مَا أَشْرَكْتُمْ وَلَا تَخَافُونَ أَنَّكُمْ أَشْرَكْتُمْ بِاللَّهِ مَا لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِ عَلَيْكُمْ سُلْطَانًا فَأَيُّ الْفَرِيقَيْنِ أَحَقُّ بِالْأَمْنِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ) (٨١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَكَيْفَ أَخَافُ): كَيْفَ is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and what governs it is أَخَافُ; it has been mentioned.
And (مَا أَشْرَكْتُمْ): «مَا» may mean الَّذِي (that which), or be an indefinite noun described by what follows, with the referring pronoun omitted; or it may be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun). (مَا لَمْ): «مَا» means الَّذِي, or is an indefinite noun described by what follows, and it is in the position of the accusative by أَشْرَكْتُمْ.
And (عَلَيْكُمْ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يُنَزِّلْ». It may also be a ḥāl from سُلْطَانًا, i.e. "that for which He has sent down no proof against you". And سُلْطَان is like رِضْوَان and كُفْرَان (in pattern). It has also been read with ḍamma on the lām, which is a dialectal form in which the ḍamma was made to follow (the preceding ḍamma).

ukberi-tibyan:82-82.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَلَمْ يَلْبِسُوا إِيمَانَهُمْ بِظُلْمٍ أُولَئِكَ لَهُمُ الْأَمْنُ وَهُمْ مُهْتَدُونَ) (٨٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): there are two views on it. One of them: it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are those who…". The second: it is a mubtadaʾ, and (أُولَئِكَ) is a badal (substitute) of it, or a second mubtadaʾ.
(لَهُمُ الْأَمْنُ): mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the clause is a khabar of what precedes it. It is also possible that الْأَمْنُ is made nominative by the preposition phrase, because it leans on what precedes it.

ukberi-tibyan:83-83.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَتِلْكَ حُجَّتُنَا آتَيْنَاهَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَى قَوْمِهِ نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَاتٍ مَنْ نَشَاءُ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ حَكِيمٌ عَلِيمٌ) (٨٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَتِلْكَ): it is a mubtadaʾ (subject). And on (حُجَّتُنَا) there are two views. One of them: it is a badal (substitute) of تِلْكَ.
And on (آتَيْنَاهَا) there are two views. One of them: it is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. And (عَلَى قَوْمِهِ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, i.e. "We gave it to Ibrāhīm as an argument against his people", or "as a proof". The second: that حُجَّتُنَا is the khabar of تِلْكَ, and آتَيْنَاهَا is in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْحُجَّة, governed by the meaning of the pointing (demonstrative). It is not permissible for عَلَى to be attached to حُجَّتُنَا, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and آتَيْنَاهَا is a khabar or a ḥāl, and neither of these may separate a relative from its ṣila. [Translator's note: the maṣdar and its complement are treated like a relative and its ṣila.]
(نَرْفَعُ): it may be in the position of the ḥāl from «آتَيْنَاهَا», or it may be resumptive. It is read with nūn and with yāʾ, and likewise نَشَاءُ; and the meaning is clear.
(دَرَجَاتٍ): it is read with the genitive construct (iḍāfa), and it is the object of نَرْفَعُ; and raising a person's rank is raising him.
It is also read with tanwīn; on this view (مَنْ) is the object of نَرْفَعُ, and «دَرَجَاتٍ» is an adverbial (ẓarf), or the preposition has been dropped from it, i.e. "to ranks".

ukberi-tibyan:84-86.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ إِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ كُلًّا هَدَيْنَا وَنُوحًا هَدَيْنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِهِ دَاوُدَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ وَأَيُّوبَ وَيُوسُفَ وَمُوسَى وَهَارُونَ وَكَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ (٨٤) وَزَكَرِيَّا وَيَحْيَى وَعِيسَى وَإِلْيَاسَ كُلٌّ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ (٨٥) وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَالْيَسَعَ وَيُونُسَ وَلُوطًا وَكُلًّا فَضَّلْنَا عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ) (٨٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كُلًّا هَدَيْنَا): كُلًّا is accusative by هَدَيْنَا, the implied form being "each of the two".
(وَنُوحًا هَدَيْنَا): i.e. "and We guided Nūḥ". The hāʾ in (ذُرِّيَّتِهِ) refers to Nūḥ, the prophets mentioned after it being the offspring of Nūḥ; the implied form is "and of his offspring We guided these".
It is also said: it refers to Ibrāhīm; but this is weak, because among them is Lūṭ, and he is not of the offspring of Ibrāhīm.
(وَكَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "and We reward the doers of good a reward like that".
As for (عِيسَى): it is said that it is foreign, with no known derivation; it is said that it is derived from al-ʿayas, which is whiteness; it is said: from al-ʿays, which is the semen of the stallion; and it is said: it is from عَاسَ يَعُوسُ, when one sets something right; on this view the yāʾ is changed from a wāw.
As for «الْيَسَعُ», it is read with a light vowelless lām and a yāʾ with fatḥa, and in it there are two views. One of them: it is a foreign proper name, and the alif and lām in it are redundant (zāʾida), as they were added in al-Nasr, which is the idol, since it is a particular idol; likewise they said ʿUmar and al-ʿUmar; and likewise al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā.
The second: that it is Arabic, being an imperfect verb used as a name, with no pronoun in it; it was declined, then made indefinite, then made definite with the alif and lām. It is also said: on this view too the lām is redundant.
And يَسَعُ: its origin is يُوسِعُ with kasra on the sīn; then the wāw was dropped because it fell between a yāʾ and a kasra; then the sīn was given fatḥa because of the guttural letter, and the wāw did not return because the fatḥa is incidental. Its like is يَطَأُ, يَقَعُ and يَدَعُ. [Translator's note: as printed; the intended form is presumably يَوْسِعُ (with fatḥa on the yāʾ).] (وَكُلًّا): accusative by فَضَّلْنَا.

ukberi-tibyan:87-87.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنْ آبَائِهِمْ وَذُرِّيَّاتِهِمْ وَإِخْوَانِهِمْ وَاجْتَبَيْنَاهُمْ وَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ) (٨٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمِنْ آبَائِهِمْ): it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «وَكُلًّا», i.e. "and We favoured some of their fathers", or "and We guided some of their fathers". [Translator's note: كُلًّا مِنْ آبَائِهِمْ, literally "each of their fathers", i.e. each of those among their fathers.]

ukberi-tibyan:88-89.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكَ هُدَى اللَّهِ يَهْدِي بِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ وَلَوْ أَشْرَكُوا لَحَبِطَ عَنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ (٨٨) أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحُكْمَ وَالنُّبُوَّةَ فَإِنْ يَكْفُرْ بِهَا هَؤُلَاءِ فَقَدْ وَكَّلْنَا بِهَا قَوْمًا لَيْسُوا بِهَا بِكَافِرِينَ) (٨٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذَلِكَ): mubtadaʾ (subject), and (هُدَى اللَّهِ) is its khabar (predicate). And (يَهْدِي بِهِ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْهُدَى, governed by the pointing (demonstrative).
It may also be a ḥāl from the name of Allah the Exalted. It is also possible that هُدَى اللَّهِ is a badal (substitute) of ذَلِكَ, with «يَهْدِي بِهِ» the khabar.
And (مِنْ عِبَادِهِ) is a ḥāl from «مَنْ» or from the omitted referring pronoun.
The bāʾ in the last «بِهَا» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «كَافِرِينَ», and the bāʾ in بِكَافِرِينَ is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "they are not disbelievers in it".

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ لِمَنْ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ قُلْ لِلَّهِ كَتَبَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ الرَّحْمَةَ لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ) (١٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِمَنْ): «مَنْ» is interrogative, and «مَا» has the meaning of الَّذِي and is in the position of a mubtadaʾ (subject), and لِمَنْ is its khabar (predicate). (قُلْ لِلَّهِ): i.e. "say: it belongs to Allah". (لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ): it is said: its position is accusative, as a badal (substitute) for الرَّحْمَةَ; and it is said: it has no position, rather it is resumptive, and the lām in it is the answer of an omitted oath, «كَتَبَ» having taken its place.
(لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ): this has been mentioned in Āl ʿImrān and al-Nisāʾ.
(الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا): a mubtadaʾ; «فَهُمْ» is a second mubtadaʾ, and (لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ) is its khabar; the second with its khabar is the khabar of the first. The fāʾ entered because of the sense of condition in الَّذِينَ. Al-Akhfash said: الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا is a badal for the accusative (pronoun) in لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ; this is far-fetched, because the pronouns of the speaker and the addressee are not substituted for, since they are as clear as can be, and other expressions fall short of them in that respect.

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَتَّخِذُ وَلِيًّا فَاطِرِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ يُطْعِمُ وَلَا يُطْعَمُ قُلْ إِنِّي أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ) (١٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ): the first object of «أَتَّخِذُ», and «وَلِيًّا» is the second.
And «أَتَّخِذُ» may be transitive to one object, which is «وَلِيًّا», with «غَيْرَ اللَّهِ» a naʿt (adjective) of it placed before it, so it became a ḥāl (circumstantial). غَيْرَ here may not be an exception.
(فَاطِرِ السَّمَاوَاتِ): it is read in the genitive, and that is the well-known reading; its genitive is as a badal (substitute) for the name of Allah. And it was read in an irregular (shādhdh) reading in the accusative, as a badal for وَلِيًّا; the meaning on this view is "shall I make the Originator of the heavens and the earth other than Allah?"
And it may be a naʿt of وَلِيًّا, with the tanwīn intended, and it is by way of quotation (ḥikāya), i.e. فَاطِرًا السَّمَاوَاتِ. [Translator's note: the source prints «فَاطِرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ» here; the intended nunated form is given.]
(وَهُوَ يُطْعِمُ): with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the ʿayn; and «وَلَا يُطْعَمُ» with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the ʿayn; this is the well-known reading. And it is read «وَلَا يَطْعَمُ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the ʿayn; and on both readings the meaning refers back to Allah.
And it was read in an irregular reading «وَهُوَ يَطْعَمُ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the ʿayn, and وَلَا يُطْعِمُ with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the ʿayn; this refers back to the patron (al-walī) who is other than Allah. (مَنْ أَسْلَمَ): i.e. "the first group that submitted".
(وَلَا تَكُونَنَّ): i.e. "and it was said to me: do not be"; had it been conjoined to what precedes, He would have said وَأَنْ لَا أَكُونَ ("and that I should not be").

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَنْ يُصْرَفْ عَنْهُ يَوْمَئِذٍ فَقَدْ رَحِمَهُ وَذَلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْمُبِينُ) (١٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَنْ يُصْرَفْ عَنْهُ): it is read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the rāʾ, as a passive (what has not had its agent named); and on what stands in place of the agent (the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)) there are two views. First: يَوْمَئِذٍ, i.e. "whoever has the punishment of that day averted from him", the muḍāf having been dropped, and يَوْمَئِذٍ is indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa.
Second: that it is latent in «يُصْرَفْ», referring back to the punishment; so يَوْمَئِذٍ is an adverb for «يُصْرَفْ», or for the punishment, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun.
And it is read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the rāʾ, with the agent named (active), i.e. "whoever Allah averts the punishment from"; on this view مَنْ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what refers back to it is the hāʾ in عَنْهُ and in «رَحِمَهُ», and the object is omitted, namely the punishment.
And the object may be «يَوْمَئِذٍ», i.e. "the punishment of that day".
And you may make «مَنْ» in the position of the accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "whoever is honoured, Allah averts from him the punishment", so «يُصْرَفْ» is made an explanation of the omitted verb; like it is (فَإِيَّايَ فَارْهَبُونِ). And مَنْ may be put in the accusative by يَصْرِفْ, with the hāʾ in عَنْهُ made to refer to the punishment, i.e. "whatever human being Allah averts the punishment from, He has had mercy on him". As for «مَنْ» on the first reading, it can only be nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the hāʾ in عَنْهُ may refer back to «مَنْ» or to the punishment.

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنْ يَمْسَسْكَ اللَّهُ بِضُرٍّ فَلَا كَاشِفَ لَهُ إِلَّا هُوَ وَإِنْ يَمْسَسْكَ بِخَيْرٍ فَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) (١٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَلَا كَاشِفَ لَهُ): «لَهُ» is the khabar (predicate) of كَاشِفَ. (إِلَّا هُوَ): a badal (substitute) for the position of «لَا كَاشِفَ», or for the pronoun in the adverbial phrase. It may not be nominative as governed by كَاشِفَ, nor a badal for a pronoun in it, because in both cases you would be making the noun of «لَا» govern, and whenever you make it govern something overt, you give it tanwīn.

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَهُوَ الْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ) (١٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَهُوَ الْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ): هُوَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and الْقَاهِرُ its khabar (predicate); and on «فَوْقَ» there are two views. First: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in الْقَاهِرُ, i.e. "and He is the Subduer, being exalted" or "prevailing".
Second: it is in the position of the nominative, as a badal (substitute) for الْقَاهِرُ or a second khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ أَيُّ شَيْءٍ أَكْبَرُ شَهَادَةً قُلِ اللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ وَأُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ هَذَا الْقُرْآنُ لِأُنْذِرَكُمْ بِهِ وَمَنْ بَلَغَ أَئِنَّكُمْ لَتَشْهَدُونَ أَنَّ مَعَ اللَّهِ آلِهَةً أُخْرَى قُلْ لَا أَشْهَدُ قُلْ إِنَّمَا هُوَ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ وَإِنَّنِي بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تُشْرِكُونَ) (١٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَيُّ شَيْءٍ): a mubtadaʾ (subject). And (أَكْبَرُ): its khabar (predicate). (شَهَادَةً): a tamyīz (specification).
And (أَيُّ) is part of what it is put in construct with; so since it is interrogative, the apparent sense requires that its answer be named by the name of what «أَيُّ» is put in construct with. This necessitates that Allah be called a "thing"; on this view His saying «قُلِ اللَّهُ» is the answer, and اللَّهُ is a mubtadaʾ with the khabar omitted, i.e. "is greatest in testimony"; and His saying «شَهِيدٌ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ.
And (اللَّهُ) may be a mubtadaʾ with شَهِيدٌ as its khabar, and this clause indicates the answer, i.e. by way of meaning. And (بَيْنَكُمْ): a repetition for emphasis, the original being شَهِيدٌ بَيْنَنَا.
You may make «بَيْنَ» an adverb governed by شَهِيدٌ, or make it a naʿt (adjective) of شَهِيدٌ, so it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted. (وَمَنْ بَلَغَ): in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the object in «أُنْذِرَكُمْ»; it has the meaning of الَّذِي, the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, and the agent is the pronoun of the Qurʾān, i.e. "and that I may warn whomever the Qurʾān reaches".
(قُلْ إِنَّمَا هُوَ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ): there are two views on «مَا». First: it is the restraining (kāffa) mā, which stops إِنَّ from governing; on this view هُوَ is a mubtadaʾ, إِلَهٌ its khabar, and وَاحِدٌ a clarifying naʿt; this has been explained in al-Baqara.
Second: that it has the meaning of الَّذِي, in the position of the accusative governed by إِنَّ; هُوَ is a mubtadaʾ and إِلَهٌ its khabar, the clause is the ṣila of الَّذِي, and وَاحِدٌ is the khabar of إِنَّ. This fits better with what precedes it.

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ يَعْرِفُونَهُ كَمَا يَعْرِفُونَ أَبْنَاءَهُمُ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ) (٢٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ): in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject).
And (يَعْرِفُونَهُ): the khabar (predicate); the hāʾ is the pronoun of the Book; it is also said: the pronoun of the Prophet ﷺ.
(الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ): like the first one.

ukberi-tibyan:152-152.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا مَالَ الْيَتِيمِ إِلَّا بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ أَشُدَّهُ وَأَوْفُوا الْكَيْلَ وَالْمِيزَانَ بِالْقِسْطِ لَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا وَإِذَا قُلْتُمْ فَاعْدِلُوا وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَا قُرْبَى وَبِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ أَوْفُوا ذَلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ) (152).
His saying (إِلَّا بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ): i.e. "except by the trait [which is best]."
(بِالْقِسْطِ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "acting with justice."
It may also be a ḥāl of the object, i.e. "give full measure, complete."
الْكَيْل ("measure") here is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of "what is measured," and الْمِيزَان likewise. It is also possible that there is an omitted muḍāf in it, its implied form being: «مَكِيلَ الْكَيْلِ» ("what is measured by the measure") and «مَوْزُونَ الْمِيزَانِ» ("what is weighed by the scale"). (لَا نُكَلِّفُ): a resumptive (new) sentence.
(وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَا قُرْبَى): i.e. "even if the one spoken to, or spoken about, were [a relative]."

ukberi-tibyan:153-153.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَأَنَّ هَذَا صِرَاطِي مُسْتَقِيمًا فَاتَّبِعُوهُ وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا السُّبُلَ فَتَفَرَّقَ بِكُمْ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ ذَلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ) (53). «[Translator's note: the verse number is printed as ٥٣ in the source; the verse is 153.]»
His saying (وَأَنَّ هَذَا): it is read with fatḥa on the hamza and the nūn doubled, and there are three views on it. The first: its implied form is "and because (وَلِأَنَّ) this …," the lām being attached to (mutaʿalliq) His saying فَاتَّبِعُوهُ, i.e. "and because of its straightness, follow it." We have mentioned something similar at His saying «كَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا».
The second: that it is conjoined to مَا حَرَّمَ, i.e. "and I recite to you that this is My path."
The third: it is conjoined to the hāʾ in وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ. This is unsound for two reasons. The first: that it is conjoined to a [genitive] pronoun without repeating the preposition.
The second: that the meaning would become "He enjoined on you the straightness of the path," which is unsound.
It is also read with fatḥa on the hamza and the nūn undoubled (وَأَنْ), and it is like the doubled one.
It is also read with kasra on the hamza (وَإِنَّ), as a resumptive (new) sentence. مُسْتَقِيمًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and what governs it is هَذَا.
(فَتَفَرَّقَ): the answer to the prohibition; the original is فَتَتَفَرَّقَ. «[Translator's note: the printed text has «وَالْأَصْلُ فَتَفَرَّقَ», which repeats the word itself; the intended original is presumably فَتَتَفَرَّقَ.]» (بِكُمْ): in the position of the object, i.e. "so that they disperse you."
It may also be a ḥāl, i.e. "so that they diverge while you are with them."

ukberi-tibyan:154-154.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ثُمَّ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ تَمَامًا عَلَى الَّذِي أَحْسَنَ وَتَفْصِيلًا لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةً لَعَلَّهُمْ بِلِقَاءِ رَبِّهِمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ) (154).
His saying (تَمَامًا): a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "We completed it, a completing." It may also be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الْكِتَاب. (عَلَى الَّذِي أَحْسَنَ): it is read with fatḥa on the nūn as a past verb, and regarding its agent there are two views. The first: the pronoun of the name of Allah, with the hāʾ omitted, i.e. "upon the one whom Allah treated well (أَحْسَنَهُ)," i.e. to whom He did good, namely Mūsā.
The second: it is the pronoun of Mūsā, because he did well in his conduct. It is also read with ḍamma on the nūn (أَحْسَنُ), as a noun, with the mubtadaʾ (subject) omitted, it being the pronoun returning to الَّذِي, i.e. "upon that which is best." «[Translator's note: the source text writes «عَلَى الَّذِي هُوَ أَحْسَنَ» with fatḥa here, though the reading described has ḍamma.]» This is weak. Some said: أَحْسَنَ, with fatḥa on the nūn, is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of الَّذِي; this is worthless, because a relative noun must have a ṣila (relative clause).
It has also been said that its implied form is: "upon those who did good (عَلَى الَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا)."

ukberi-tibyan:155-155.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَهَذَا كِتَابٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ مُبَارَكٌ فَاتَّبِعُوهُ وَاتَّقُوا لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ) (155).
His saying (وَهَذَا): a mubtadaʾ (subject); «كِتَابٌ» is its khabar (predicate), and «أَنْزَلْنَاهُ» is an adjective or a second khabar. «مُبَارَكٌ» is a second adjective or a third khabar. Had it been read «مُبَارَكًا», accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), it would have been permissible.

ukberi-tibyan:156-156.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَنْ تَقُولُوا إِنَّمَا أُنْزِلَ الْكِتَابُ عَلَى طَائِفَتَيْنِ مِنْ قَبْلِنَا وَإِنْ كُنَّا عَنْ دِرَاسَتِهِمْ لَغَافِلِينَ) (156).
His saying (أَنْ تَقُولُوا): i.e. "We sent it down out of aversion to your saying."
(أَوْ تَقُولُوا): conjoined to it. (وَإِنْ كُنَّا): إِنْ is lightened from the heavy form (إِنَّ), and the lām in «لَغَافِلِينَ» is a compensation, or distinguishes between [the lightened] إِنْ and [the negative] مَا. «[Translator's note: the printed text has «بَيْنَ إِنَّ وَمَا».]»

ukberi-tibyan:157-157.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَوْ تَقُولُوا لَوْ أَنَّا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْنَا الْكِتَابُ لَكُنَّا أَهْدَى مِنْهُمْ فَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ بَيِّنَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةٌ فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنْ كَذَّبَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ وَصَدَفَ عَنْهَا سَنَجْزِي الَّذِينَ يَصْدِفُونَ عَنْ آيَاتِنَا سُوءَ الْعَذَابِ بِمَا كَانُوا يَصْدِفُونَ) (157).
His saying (مِمَّنْ كَذَّبَ): the majority read it doubled; it has been read undoubled (كَذَبَ), and that has the meaning of the doubled one, so that بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ is an object. It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "he lied while the signs of Allah were with him."
(يَصْدِفُونَ): it is read with a pure ṣād, according to the base form; with the ṣād given a tinge of zāy (ishmām); and with it turned completely into zāy (يَزْدِفُونَ), so that it comes close to the dāl. What made that permissible in it is its being quiescent.

ukberi-tibyan:158-158.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ أَوْ يَأْتِيَ رَبُّكَ أَوْ يَأْتِيَ بَعْضُ آيَاتِ رَبِّكَ يَوْمَ يَأْتِي بَعْضُ آيَاتِ رَبِّكَ لَا يَنْفَعُ نَفْسًا إِيمَانُهَا لَمْ تَكُنْ آمَنَتْ مِنْ قَبْلُ أَوْ كَسَبَتْ فِي إِيمَانِهَا خَيْرًا قُلِ انْتَظِرُوا إِنَّا مُنْتَظِرُونَ) (158).
His saying (يَوْمَ يَأْتِي): the majority read it in the accusative, and what governs the adverb is «لَا يَنْفَعُ». It has been read in the nominative (يَوْمُ), with the khabar (predicate) being لَا يَنْفَعُ and the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "«نَفْسًا إِيمَانُهَا» does not benefit … in it."
The majority read يَنْفَعُ with yāʾ. It has been read with tāʾ (تَنْفَعُ), and there are two views on it.
The first: that the maṣdar (verbal noun) was made feminine according to the meaning, because الْإِيمَان ("faith") and الْعَقِيدَة ("creed") have one meaning; it is like their saying: جَاءَتْهُ كِتَابِي فَاحْتَقَرَهَا ("my letter came to him and he scorned it"), i.e. my page or my message.
The second: that the feminine was acceptable because of the annexation to a feminine noun.
(لَمْ تَكُنْ): there are two views on it. The first: it is a resumptive (new) sentence. The second: it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the genitive pronoun, or as an adjective of نَفْس; and this is weak.

ukberi-tibyan:159-159.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ فَرَّقُوا دِينَهُمْ وَكَانُوا شِيَعًا لَسْتَ مِنْهُمْ فِي شَيْءٍ إِنَّمَا أَمْرُهُمْ إِلَى اللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِمَا كَانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ) (159).
His saying (فَرَّقُوا دِينَهُمْ): it is read doubled without alif, and undoubled (فَرَقُوا), which has the meaning of the doubled one.
It is also possible that the meaning is "they separated it from the true religion." It is also read فَارَقُوا, i.e. "they abandoned."
(لَسْتَ مِنْهُمْ فِي شَيْءٍ): i.e. "you are not in anything that is from them."

ukberi-tibyan:160-160.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مَنْ جَاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا وَمَنْ جَاءَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ فَلَا يُجْزَى إِلَّا مِثْلَهَا وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ) (160).
His saying (عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا): it is read with annexation (iḍāfa), i.e. "he will have ten good deeds like it," the adjective being sufficient [in place of the noun].
It is also read in the nominative with tanwīn (عَشْرٌ أَمْثَالُهَا), on the implied form "he will have ten good deeds, like it"; the tāʾ was dropped from عَشْر because الْأَمْثَال is feminine in meaning, since the like of a good deed is a good deed.
It has also been said that it was treated as feminine because it was annexed to a feminine noun.

ukberi-tibyan:161-161.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ إِنَّنِي هَدَانِي رَبِّي إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ دِينًا قِيَمًا مِلَّةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ حَنِيفًا وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ) (161).
His saying (دِينًا): there are three views on its accusative. It is a badal (substitute) of الصِّرَاط according to its position, because the meaning of هَدَانِي and عَرَّفَنِي ("He made me know") is one. It has also been said: accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "He made me know a religion." The third: that it is the object of هَدَانِي, هَدَى being transitive to two objects. «قَيِّمًا», doubled, is an adjective of دِين; it is also read undoubled (قِيَمًا), and this has been mentioned in al-Nisāʾ and al-Māʾida. (مِلَّةَ): a badal of دِين, or on the implication of "I mean" (أَعْنِي). (حَنِيفًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial), or on the implication of "I mean."

ukberi-tibyan:162-162.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ إِنَّ صَلَاتِي وَنُسُكِي وَمَحْيَايَ وَمَمَاتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ) (163). «[Translator's note: the source numbers this verse ١٦٣; it is verse 162.]»
His saying (وَمَحْيَايَ): the majority read the yāʾ with fatḥa, and its original state is fatḥa, because it is a pronoun particle, like the kāf in رَأَيْتُكَ and the tāʾ in قُمْتُ. It has been read with it quiescent (وَمَحْيَايْ), as it is made quiescent in «أَيْ» and the like; that is permitted even though a quiescent letter precedes it, because the long vowel separates the two. In the irregular (shādhdh) readings it has been read with kasra on the yāʾ (وَمَحْيَايِ), on the view that it is a pronoun given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. (لِلَّهِ): i.e. "all of that is for Allah."

ukberi-tibyan:164-164.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَبْغِي رَبًّا وَهُوَ رَبُّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ).
His saying (قُلْ أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ): it is like His saying (وَمَنْ يَبْتَغِ غَيْرَ الْإِسْلَامِ), which has been discussed.

ukberi-tibyan:165-165.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَكُمْ خَلَائِفَ الْأَرْضِ وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَكُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجَاتٍ لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ فِي مَا آتَاكُمْ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ سَرِيعُ الْعِقَابِ وَإِنَّهُ لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) (165).
His saying (دَرَجَاتٍ): this has been discussed at His saying (نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَاتٍ مَنْ نَشَاءُ).

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَوْمَ نَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ نَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا أَيْنَ شُرَكَاؤُكُمُ الَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تَزْعُمُونَ) (٢٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَيَوْمَ نَحْشُرُهُمْ): it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the implied wording is "and remember the day We gather them". And (جَمِيعًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object pronoun. The two objects of «تَزْعُمُونَ» are omitted, i.e. "you claimed them to be your partners", what precedes indicating the omitted elements.

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ فِتْنَتُهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ قَالُوا وَاللَّهِ رَبِّنَا مَا كُنَّا مُشْرِكِينَ) (٢٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ): it is read with tāʾ, and الْفِتْنَةُ in the nominative as the noun of kāna.
And (أَنْ قَالُوا) is the khabar (predicate). And it is read the same way except with yāʾ, because the femininity of الْفِتْنَةُ is not real, and because الْفِتْنَةُ here has the meaning of "saying". And it is read with yāʾ and الْفِتْنَةَ in the accusative, on the view that the noun of kāna is «أَنْ قَالُوا» and «فِتْنَتَهُمْ» is the khabar.
And it is read the same way except with tāʾ, according to the meaning of أَنْ قَالُوا, because أَنْ قَالُوا has the meaning of "the saying", "the statement" and "the trial (fitna)". (رَبِّنَا): it is read in the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of the name of Allah, and in the accusative as a vocative, or by implying أَعْنِي ("I mean"); it is parenthetical between the oath and what is sworn to. The answer (of the oath) is مَا كُنَّا.

ukberi-tibyan:25-25.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيْكَ وَجَعَلْنَا عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً أَنْ يَفْقَهُوهُ وَفِي آذَانِهِمْ وَقْرًا وَإِنْ يَرَوْا كُلَّ آيَةٍ لَا يُؤْمِنُوا بِهَا حَتَّى إِذَا جَاءُوكَ يُجَادِلُونَكَ يَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ هَذَا إِلَّا أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ) (٢٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُ): the pronoun in the verb is made singular, construed according to the wording of «مَنْ»; and where it comes in the plural form, it is according to the meaning of «مَنْ», as in (مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُونَ) and (مَنْ يَغُوصُونَ لَهُ).
(أَنْ يَفْقَهُوهُ): a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "out of aversion that they should understand it".
And (وَقْرًا): conjoined to أَكِنَّةً; the separation between the conjunction and the conjoined noun by the adverbial phrase does not count as a separation, because the adverbial is one of the objects, so it may be placed before or after. الْوَقْرُ is singular here because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun); the discussion of it has been given in full at the beginning of al-Baqara. (حَتَّى إِذَا): إِذَا is in the position of the accusative governed by its answer, which is يَقُولُ; حَتَّى here has no governing effect; it only conveys the meaning of limit (ghāya), just as it does not govern clauses. And (يُجَادِلُونَكَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in جَاءُوكَ.
الْأَسَاطِيرُ is a plural, and there is disagreement about its singular. It is said: it is أُسْطُورَةٌ; and it is said: its singular is أَسْطَارٌ, and أَسْطَارٌ is the plural of سَطَرٌ with a vowel on the ṭāʾ, so أَسَاطِيرُ is a plural of a plural. As for سَطْرٌ with a quiescent ṭāʾ, its plural is سُطُورٌ and أَسْطُرٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَهُمْ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ وَيَنْأَوْنَ عَنْهُ وَإِنْ يُهْلِكُونَ إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ) (٢٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَيَنْأَوْنَ): it is read with the nūn quiescent and the hamza pronounced fully, and with the vowel of the hamza cast onto the nūn and the hamza dropped, so that its pronunciation becomes «يُنَوَّنُ» [Translator's note: so printed; the form described is يَنَوْنَ], with fatḥa on the nūn and a quiescent wāw after it. And (أَنْفُسَهُمْ): the object of يُهْلِكُونَ.

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْ تَرَى إِذْ وُقِفُوا عَلَى النَّارِ فَقَالُوا يَا لَيْتَنَا نُرَدُّ وَلَا نُكَذِّبَ بِآيَاتِ رَبِّنَا وَنَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) (٢٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَوْ تَرَى): the answer of «لَوْ» is omitted, its implied form being "you would have witnessed a tremendous matter".
And وُقِفَ is transitive [Translator's note: so printed; the active وَقَفَ is presumably meant], and أَوْقَفَ is a weak dialectal form; the Qurʾān came without the alif, and from it is وُقِفُوا, built as a passive (what has not had its agent named), and from it also is «وَقِفُوهُمْ». «وَلَا نُكَذِّبَ» and «وَنَكُونَ» are read in the nominative, and there are two views on it. First: it is conjoined to نُرَدُّ, so not denying and being among the believers are also wished for, like the return.
Second: that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "and we will not deny"; and on the meaning there are two views. First: that it is also wished for, so it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «نُرَدُّ».
Second: that the meaning is that they guaranteed not to deny after being returned, so the clause has no grammatical position. And both are read in the accusative, as the answer of the wish, so it is not included in the wish; and the wāw in this is like the fāʾ.
Among the readers are those who read the first in the nominative and the second in the accusative, and among them are those who did the reverse; and the explanation of each of them is according to what has preceded.

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالُوا إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا حَيَاتُنَا الدُّنْيَا وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَبْعُوثِينَ) (٢٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا): هِيَ is an allusive pronoun referring to the life; and it may be the pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa).

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْ تَرَى إِذْ وُقِفُوا عَلَى رَبِّهِمْ قَالَ أَلَيْسَ هَذَا بِالْحَقِّ قَالُوا بَلَى وَرَبِّنَا قَالَ فَذُوقُوا الْعَذَابَ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ) (٣٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وُقِفُوا عَلَى رَبِّهِمْ): i.e. "for their Lord's questioning", or "at their Lord's dominion".

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَدْ خَسِرَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِلِقَاءِ اللَّهِ حَتَّى إِذَا جَاءَتْهُمُ السَّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً قَالُوا يَا حَسْرَتَنَا عَلَى مَا فَرَّطْنَا فِيهَا وَهُمْ يَحْمِلُونَ أَوْزَارَهُمْ عَلَى ظُهُورِهِمْ أَلَا سَاءَ مَا يَزِرُونَ) (٣١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَغْتَةً): a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "coming suddenly".
It is also said: it is a maṣdar of an omitted verb, i.e. "taking them suddenly, a sudden taking".
It is also said: it is a maṣdar (governed) by جَاءَتْهُمْ, not of its own root.
(يَاحَسْرَتَنَا): calling upon regret and woe figuratively; the implied wording is "O regret, come; this is your time"; and the meaning is alerting themselves so that they recall the causes of regret.
And (عَلَى): attached (mutaʿalliq) to الْحَسْرَةِ; the pronoun in «فِيهَا» refers back to the Hour, and the implied wording is "in working for the Hour".
It is also said: it refers back to the deeds, which have not been explicitly mentioned, but there is an indication of them in the speech.
(أَلَا سَاءَ مَا يَزِرُونَ): «سَاءَ» has the meaning of بِئْسَ ("how evil"), and its i'rab has preceded in several places. And سَاءَ may be in its usual sense, with the object omitted, and مَا maṣdariyya (infinitival), or with the meaning of الَّذِي, or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa); in all of these it is the fāʿil (agent) of سَاءَ, and the implied wording is "indeed, their burden grieves them".

ukberi-tibyan:90-90.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ هَدَى اللَّهُ فَبِهُدَاهُمُ اقْتَدِهِ قُلْ لَا أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْرًا إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرَى لِلْعَالَمِينَ) (٩٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (اقْتَدِهِ): it is read with sukūn on the hāʾ, kept when pausing but not in continuous recitation; on this view it is the hāʾ of pausing (hāʾ al-sakt). Some keep it in continuous recitation too, because of its resemblance to the pronoun hāʾ.
Some give it kasra, and in that there are two views. One of them: it is also the hāʾ of pausing, likened to the pronoun hāʾ; but this is nothing (of no weight).
The second: it is the pronoun hāʾ, and what it refers to is the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "follow the following". Its like is:
هَذَا سُرَاقَةُ لِلْقُرْآنِ يَدْرُسُهُ ... وَالْمَرْءُ عِنْدَ الرُّشَا إِنْ يَلْقَهَا ذِيبُ
("This is Surāqa — he studies (it) the Quran; yet a man, when he meets with bribes, is a wolf.")
So the hāʾ is the pronoun of the studying, not an object, because يَدْرُسُ has already been made transitive to الْقُرْآن (by the lām).
It is also said: whoever gives the hāʾ sukūn makes it the pronoun hāʾ, and treats continuous recitation like pausing. The hāʾ in (عَلَيْهِ) is the pronoun of the Quran and of the conveying of the message.

ukberi-tibyan:91-91.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ إِذْ قَالُوا مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَى بَشَرٍ مِنْ شَيْءٍ قُلْ مَنْ أَنْزَلَ الْكِتَابَ الَّذِي جَاءَ بِهِ مُوسَى نُورًا وَهُدًى لِلنَّاسِ تَجْعَلُونَهُ قَرَاطِيسَ تُبْدُونَهَا وَتُخْفُونَ كَثِيرًا وَعُلِّمْتُمْ مَا لَمْ تَعْلَمُوا أَنْتُمْ وَلَا آبَاؤُكُمْ قُلِ اللَّهُ ثُمَّ ذَرْهُمْ فِي خَوْضِهِمْ يَلْعَبُونَ) (٩١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ): حَقَّ is accusative in the way a maṣdar (verbal noun) is accusative. It is originally an adjective, i.e. "His true estimation"; and the adjective of a maṣdar, when put in construct with it, is accusative in the way the maṣdar is.
(قَدْرِهِ) is read with sukūn on the dāl and with fatḥa. And (إِذْ) is an adverbial (ẓarf) of قَدَرُوا. And (مِنْ شَيْءٍ) is the object of أَنْزَلَ, مِنْ being redundant (zāʾida).
(نُورًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «بِهِ» or from الْكِتَاب; and بِهِ may be a mafʿūl bihi (object), or a ḥāl. And (تَجْعَلُونَهُ) is resumptive, with no grammatical position. And (قَرَاطِيسَ): i.e. "in sheets"; it is also said: "consisting of sheets".
It is also said: there is no omitted element implied in it, and the meaning is that they treated it like sheets with nothing in them, in neglecting to act on it.
And (تُبْدُونَهَا) is a description of الْقَرَاطِيس; «وَتُخْفُونَ» likewise, the implied form being "and you conceal much of them".
It is read in the three places with yāʾ, in the third person, construed according to what precedes it at the beginning of the verse; and with tāʾ, in the second person, which suits His saying «وَعُلِّمْتُمْ», i.e. "and you have been taught". The clause is in the position of the ḥāl from the agent pronoun in تَجْعَلُونَهُ on the tāʾ reading.
On the yāʾ reading, وَعُلِّمْتُمْ may be resumptive, or He may have turned from the third person to the second. And (قُلِ اللَّهُ) is the answer to «قُلْ مَنْ أَنْزَلَ الْكِتَابَ»; it is nominative by an omitted verb, i.e. "Allah sent it down".
It is also possible that the implied form is "He is Allah", or "the one who sent down is Allah", or "Allah sent it down".
(فِي خَوْضِهِمْ): it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to ذَرْهُمْ as an adverbial of it; or a ḥāl from the object pronoun, i.e. "leave them plunging"; or attached to «يَلْعَبُونَ».
(يَلْعَبُونَ) is in the position of the ḥāl, the one it describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl) being the object pronoun in ذَرْهُمْ, if فِي خَوْضِهِمْ is not made a ḥāl from it; and if you make it a ḥāl from it, the second ḥāl is from the pronoun of settledness (istiqrār) in the first ḥāl.
It may also be a ḥāl from the genitive pronoun in خَوْضِهِمْ, the governor being the maṣdar, the genitive pronoun being an agent in meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:92-92.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَهَذَا كِتَابٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ مُبَارَكٌ مُصَدِّقُ الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَلِتُنْذِرَ أُمَّ الْقُرَى وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ وَهُمْ عَلَى صَلَاتِهِمْ يُحَافِظُونَ) (٩٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْزَلْنَاهُ): in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of كِتَابٌ. And (مُبَارَكٌ) is another naʿt; the description by a clause has been put before the description by a single word. In other than the Quran the accusative would be permissible, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object pronoun, or as a ḥāl from the described indefinite noun. And (مُصَدِّقُ الَّذِي): the tanwīn is considered as present, because the genitive construct is not pure (ghayr maḥḍa).
(وَلِتُنْذِرَ): with tāʾ, addressing the Prophet ﷺ; and with yāʾ, the agent being the Book. There is an omission in the sentence, its implied form being "so that they may believe and so that you may warn", or the like; or "so that you may warn «أُمَّ الْقُرَى» We sent it down".
(وَمَنْ): in the position of the accusative, maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «أُمَّ»; the implied form is "and so that you may warn the people of the Mother (of towns)".
(وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ): mubtadaʾ (subject), and «يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ» is the khabar (predicate).
It is also possible that الَّذِينَ is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to أُمَّ الْقُرَى, so that يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ is a ḥāl. And (عَلَى) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يُحَافِظُونَ».

ukberi-tibyan:93-93.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا أَوْ قَالَ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ وَلَمْ يُوحَ إِلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ وَمَنْ قَالَ سَأُنْزِلُ مِثْلَ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ وَلَوْ تَرَى إِذِ الظَّالِمُونَ فِي غَمَرَاتِ الْمَوْتِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ بَاسِطُو أَيْدِيهِمْ أَخْرِجُوا أَنْفُسَكُمُ الْيَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ عَذَابَ الْهُونِ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ وَكُنْتُمْ عَنْ آيَاتِهِ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ) (٩٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا): «كَذِبًا» may be the object of افْتَرَى; or a maṣdar (verbal noun) according to the meaning, i.e. "an inventing"; or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); or a maṣdar in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial).
(أَوْ قَالَ): conjoined to افْتَرَى. And (إِلَيَّ) is in the position of the nominative, standing in the place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent). It may also be in the position of the accusative, the implied form being "(it) revealed the revelation" or "the revealing". [Translator's note: so in the text («أَوْحَى»); the sense is that the deputy agent is the implied maṣdar, "the revelation was revealed to me".]
(وَلَمْ يُوحَ إِلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ): in the position of the ḥāl from the agent pronoun in قَالَ, or from the yāʾ in إِلَيَّ. (وَمَنْ قَالَ): in the position of the genitive, conjoined to مَنِ افْتَرَى, i.e. "and than one who said".
And (مِثْلَ مَا) may be the object of سَأُنْزِلُ, مَا meaning الَّذِي (that which) or being an indefinite noun described by what follows.
It may also be a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, مَا being maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun).
And (إِذْ) is an adverbial (ẓarf) of تَرَى, and the object is omitted, i.e. "if you could see the disbelievers", or the like.
And (الظَّالِمُونَ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the ẓarf after it is its khabar (predicate); الْمَلَائِكَةُ is a mubtadaʾ, and what follows it is the khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl from the pronoun in the khabar before it.
And (بَاسِطُوا أَيْدِيهِمْ) is to be understood with tanwīn, i.e. بَاسِطُونَ أَيْدِيهِمْ. (أَخْرِجُوا): i.e. "saying: bring out…"; and the omitted element is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «بَاسِطُو».
And (الْيَوْمَ) is an adverbial of أَخْرِجُوا, so the pause is complete on it.
It may also be an adverbial of «تُجْزَوْنَ», so the pause is complete on «أَنْفُسَكُمُ».
(غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ): the object of تَقُولُونَ.
It may also be a description of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a saying other than the truth".
(وَكُنْتُمْ): it may be conjoined to the first «كُنْتُمْ», i.e. "and because you were…", or it may be resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:94-94.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا فُرَادَى كَمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَتَرَكْتُمْ مَا خَوَّلْنَاكُمْ وَرَاءَ ظُهُورِكُمْ وَمَا نَرَى مَعَكُمْ شُفَعَاءَكُمُ الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ أَنَّهُمْ فِيكُمْ شُرَكَاءُ لَقَدْ تَقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ وَضَلَّ عَنْكُمْ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَزْعُمُونَ) (٩٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فُرَادَى): it is the plural of فَرْد, and the alif is for the feminine, like كُسَالَى.
It has been read, among the irregular (shādhdh) readings, with tanwīn, as a sound noun (ism ṣaḥīḥ). In the nominative one says فُرَادٌ, like تُوَامٌ and رُخَالٌ; and it is a rare plural.
Some do not decline it fully, making it a deflected form (maʿdūl), like ثُلَاثَ and رُبَاعَ. It is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun.
(كَمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ): the kāf is in the position of the ḥāl, and it is a badal (substitute) of فُرَادَى. It is also said: it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a coming like your coming the day We created you". It may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun in فُرَادَى, i.e. "resembling the beginning of your creation".
And (أَوَّلَ) is an adverbial (ẓarf) of خَلَقْنَاكُمْ. And «الْمَرَّة» is originally the maṣdar of مَرَّ يَمُرُّ; then it was used as an adverbial by extension; this shows the strength of the resemblance of time to the verb. (وَتَرَكْتُمْ): it may be a ḥāl, i.e. "having left", or resumptive.
(وَمَا نَرَى): its wording is that of the imperfect, and it is a narration of a past state (ḥikāyat ḥāl). And (مَعَكُمْ) is governed by نَرَى, which is from seeing with the eye. It may not be a ḥāl from الشُّفَعَاء, since the meaning would become that their intercessors are with them but We do not see them.
If you make it mean "We know", transitive to two objects, مَعَكُمْ may be the second object; but this is weak in meaning. (بَيْنَكُمْ): it is read in the accusative, and in this there are three views. One of them: it is an adverbial of «تَقَطَّعَ», the agent being implied, i.e. "the bond between you has been cut", «شُرَكَاءُ» indicating it. The second: it is a description of something omitted, i.e. "something between you has been cut", or "a bond".
The third: that this accusative form is in the position of the nominative and is declinable; that was permitted by construing it according to the most frequent states of the adverbial. This is the view of al-Akhfash; and its like is (مِنَّا الصَّالِحُونَ وَمِنَّا دُونَ ذَلِكَ).
It is also read in the nominative as the agent. Al-bayn here is "the bond", and it is one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād).

ukberi-tibyan:95-96.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ فَالِقُ الْحَبِّ وَالنَّوَى يُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ وَمُخْرِجُ الْمَيِّتِ مِنَ الْحَيِّ ذَلِكُمُ اللَّهُ فَأَنَّى تُؤْفَكُونَ (٩٥) فَالِقُ الْإِصْبَاحِ وَجَعَلَ اللَّيْلَ سَكَنًا وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ حُسْبَانًا ذَلِكَ تَقْدِيرُ الْعَزِيزِ الْعَلِيمِ) (٩٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَالِقُ الْحَبِّ): it may be definite, because it is past; or indefinite, as the narration of a state (ḥikāyat ḥāl).
It has been read, irregularly (shādhdh), «فَلَقَ». And «الْإِصْبَاحِ» is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of أَصْبَحَ.
It is also read with fatḥa on the hamza, as the plural of صُبْح, like قُفْل and أَقْفَال.
(وَجَاعِلُ اللَّيْلَ): like فَالِقُ الْإِصْبَاحِ in the two views.
And (سَكَنًا) is the object of جَاعِلُ if you do not treat it as definite; if you treat it as definite, it is accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "He made it a rest". السَّكَن is that in which you find repose, such as family and the like; so He made the night like family. It is also said: the implied form is "rested in", or "possessing rest".
And (الشَّمْسَ) is accusative by an omitted verb, or by جَاعِلُ if you do not treat it as definite.
It has been read, irregularly, in the genitive, conjoined to الْإِصْبَاحِ or to اللَّيْلِ.
And on (حُسْبَانًا) there are two views. One of them: it is the plural of حُسْبَانَة. The second: it is a maṣdar like الْحَسْب and الْحِسَاب; and its accusative is like the accusative of سَكَنًا.

ukberi-tibyan:98-98.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَنْشَأَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ فَمُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمُسْتَوْدَعٌ قَدْ فَصَّلْنَا الْآيَاتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَفْقَهُونَ) (٩٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَمُسْتَقَرٌّ): it is read with fatḥa on the qāf, and in this there are two views. One of them: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "then for you there is a settling".
The second: that it is a passive participle, by which the place is meant, i.e. "then for you there is a place in which you settle", either in the wombs or in the graves. It is also read with kasra on the qāf, so it is a place that settles for you. It is also said: its implied form is "then of you there is one who settles".
As for (مُسْتَوْدَعٌ), it is with fatḥa on the dāl only. It may be a place in which they are deposited, which is either the loins or the grave.
It may also be a maṣdar meaning "depositing".

ukberi-tibyan:99-99.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ نَبَاتَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ فَأَخْرَجْنَا مِنْهُ خَضِرًا نُخْرِجُ مِنْهُ حَبًّا مُتَرَاكِبًا وَمِنَ النَّخْلِ مِنْ طَلْعِهَا قِنْوَانٌ دَانِيَةٌ وَجَنَّاتٍ مِنْ أَعْنَابٍ وَالزَّيْتُونَ وَالرُّمَّانَ مُشْتَبِهًا وَغَيْرَ مُتَشَابِهٍ انْظُرُوا إِلَى ثَمَرِهِ إِذَا أَثْمَرَ وَيَنْعِهِ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكُمْ لَآيَاتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ) (٩٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَأَخْرَجْنَا مِنْهُ خَضِرًا): i.e. "by means of it"; and الْخَضِر means الْأَخْضَر (green).
It is also possible that the hāʾ in مِنْهُ refers back to النَّبَات, and this is the more likely. On the first view, فَأَخْرَجْنَا is a badal (substitute) of the first أَخْرَجْنَا.
(نُخْرِجُ): in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of خَضِرًا; it may also be resumptive. And the hāʾ in (مِنْهُ) refers back to الْخَضِر.
And (قِنْوَانٌ): with kasra on the qāf and with ḍamma; they are two dialectal forms, and both have been read. Its singular is قِنْو, like صِنْو and صِنْوَان. On its nominative there are two views. One of them: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and on its khabar (predicate) there are two views. One of them: it is وَمِنَ النَّخْلِ, and مِنْ طَلْعِهَا is a badal with repetition of the preposition.
The second: that the khabar is «مِنْ طَلْعِهَا», and in مِنَ النَّخْلِ there is a pronoun, its implied form being "and there grew from the palms something" or "fruit", so that مِنْ طَلْعِهَا is a badal of it.
The other view: that قِنْوَانٌ is nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of مِنْ طَلْعِهَا; then in مِنَ النَّخْلِ there is a pronoun explained by قِنْوَانٌ. And if you make قِنْوَانٌ nominative by His saying «وَمِنَ النَّخْلِ», according to the view of those who give government to the first of two verbs, it is permissible, and in مِنْ طَلْعِهَا there is a nominative pronoun. It has been read, irregularly (shādhdh), قَنْوَانٌ with fatḥa on the qāf; this is not a plural of قِنْو, because the pattern faʿlān is not a plural; it is only a collective noun (ism jamʿ), like الْبَاقِر.
(وَجَنَّاتٍ): in the accusative, conjoined to His saying «نَبَاتَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ», i.e. "and We brought forth by it gardens"; and likewise «وَالزَّيْتُونَ وَالرُّمَّانَ».
It is also read with ḍamma on the tāʾ, as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, the implied form being "and of the vine there are gardens".
It may not be conjoined to قِنْوَانٌ, because grapes do not come out of palm trees. And «مِنْ أَعْنَابٍ» is a naʿt of جَنَّاتٍ. And (مُشْتَبِهًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الرُّمَّان, or from all of them.
And (إِذَا) is an adverbial (ẓarf) of انْظُرُوا.
And (ثَمَرِهِ): it is read with fatḥa on the thāʾ and the mīm, as the plural of ثَمَرَة, like تَمْرَة and تَمْر; in strict analysis it is a generic noun, not a plural. It is also read with ḍamma on the thāʾ and the mīm, as the plural of ثَمَرَة, like خَشَبَة and خُشُب. It is also said: it is the plural of ثِمَار, like كِتَاب and كُتُب, so it is a plural of a plural; as for ثِمَار, its singular is ثَمَرَة, like خَيْمَة and خِيَام.
It is also said: it is the plural of ثَمَر.
It is also read with ḍamma on the thāʾ and sukūn on the mīm, lightened from the form with ḍamma.
(وَيَنْعِهِ): it is read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and with ḍamma; they are two dialectal forms, and both are the maṣdar of يَنَعَتِ الثَّمَرَةُ ("the fruit ripened").
It is also said: it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar), the verb being أَيْنَعَتْ إِينَاعًا. It is read, irregularly, «يَانِعِهِ», as an active participle.

ukberi-tibyan:100-100.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكَاءَ الْجِنَّ وَخَلَقَهُمْ وَخَرَقُوا لَهُ بَنِينَ وَبَنَاتٍ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ) (١٠٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَجَعَلُوا): it has the meaning of صَبَرُوا [Translator's note: so printed; evidently a misprint for «صَيَّرُوا», "they made (into)"], and its first object is «الْجِنَّ» and the second «شُرَكَاءَ». And لِلَّهِ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to شُرَكَاءَ; it may also be a naʿt (adjective) of شُرَكَاءَ put before it, so it became a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is also possible that the first object is شُرَكَاءَ, with الْجِنَّ a badal (substitute) of it, and لِلَّهِ the second object.
(وَخَلَقَهُمْ): i.e. "when He had created them", so the clause is a ḥāl. It is also said: it is resumptive.
It has been read, irregularly (shādhdh), «وَخَلْقَهُمْ», with sukūn on the lām and fatḥa on the qāf; the implied form is "and they made the God of their creation partners". (وَخَرَقُوا): without shadda, and with shadda for intensiveness.
(بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ): in the position of the ḥāl from the agent in خَرَقُوا; it may also be a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a fabricating without knowledge".

ukberi-tibyan:101-101.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (بَدِيعُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ أَنَّى يَكُونُ لَهُ وَلَدٌ وَلَمْ تَكُنْ لَهُ صَاحِبَةٌ وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ) (١٠١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَدِيعُ السَّمَاوَاتِ): on its nominative there are three views. First: it is the fāʿil (agent) of «تَعَالَى». Second: it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "He is the Originator".
Third: it is a mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is «أَنَّى يَكُونُ لَهُ» and what is connected with it.
And (أَنَّى) means "how" or "from where"; its position is that of a ḥāl (circumstantial); the one it describes is «وَلَدٌ», and the governor is يَكُونُ.
It (يَكُونُ) may be complete (tāmma) or incomplete (nāqiṣa).
(وَلَمْ تَكُنْ): it is read with tāʾ, treating الصَّاحِبَة as feminine.
It is also read with yāʾ, and in this there are three views. First: that it is for الصَّاحِبَة, but the masculine was permitted since there is a separation between the two.
Second: that the noun of كَانَ is the pronoun of the name of Allah, and the clause is its khabar, i.e. "and Allah has not had for Him His consort". [Translator's note: so printed («وَلَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لَهُ صَاحِبَتُهُ»); the sense is "and Allah was not such that He had a consort".] Third: that the noun of كَانَ is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause explains it.

ukberi-tibyan:102-102.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ فَاعْبُدُوهُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَكِيلٌ) (١٠٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذَلِكُمْ): a mubtadaʾ (subject); and on the khabar (predicate) there are several views. First: it is «اللَّهُ»; (رَبُّكُمْ) is a second khabar, «لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ» a third, and «خَالِقُ كُلِّ» a fourth. Second: that the khabar is «اللَّهُ» and what follows it is substitutes (badal) of it. Third: that «اللَّهُ» is a badal of ذَلِكُمْ, and the khabar is what follows it.

ukberi-tibyan:104-104.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَدْ جَاءَكُمْ بَصَائِرُ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فَمَنْ أَبْصَرَ فَلِنَفْسِهِ وَمَنْ عَمِيَ فَعَلَيْهَا وَمَا أَنَا عَلَيْكُمْ بِحَفِيظٍ) (١٠٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَدْ جَاءَكُمْ بَصَائِرُ): the feminine tāʾ was not attached to the verb because of the separation by the object, and because the femininity of the agent is not real. [Translator's note: the text reads «لِلْفَصْلِ بَيْنَ الْمَفْعُولِ», apparently with words missing, i.e. "the separation (between verb and agent) by the object".]
And (مِنْ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to جَاءَ; it may also be a naʿt (adjective) of الْبَصَائِر, and so be attached to something omitted.
(فَمَنْ أَبْصَرَ): مَنْ is a mubtadaʾ (subject). It may be conditional, in which case the khabar (predicate) is أَبْصَرَ, and the apodosis (jawāb) of مَنْ is «فَعَلَيْهَا». [Translator's note: so in the text; for «فَمَنْ أَبْصَرَ» the apodosis is «فَلِنَفْسِهِ», while «فَعَلَيْهَا» answers «وَمَنْ عَمِيَ».]
It may also mean الَّذِي (the one who), in which case what follows the fāʾ is the khabar, with its mubtadaʾ omitted, its implied form being "then his seeing is for himself"; and likewise His saying «وَمَنْ عَمِيَ فَعَلَيْهَا».

ukberi-tibyan:105-105.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَذَلِكَ نُصَرِّفُ الْآيَاتِ وَلِيَقُولُوا دَرَسْتَ وَلِنُبَيِّنَهُ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ) (١٠٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَكَذَلِكَ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "«نُصَرِّفُ الْآيَاتِ» a varying like that with which We have recited them to you". (وَلِيَقُولُوا): i.e. "and so that they would say 'you have studied', We varied (them)"; and the lām is the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba), i.e. their affair ends in this. It is also said: He intended by the varying that they should say «دَرَسْتَ», as a punishment for them.
(دَارَسْتَ): it is read with alif and fatḥa on the tāʾ, i.e. "you have studied with the People of the Book".
It is read likewise but without alif, i.e. "you have studied the earlier books".
It is read likewise but with shadda, and the meaning is like the first meaning. It is also read with ḍamma on the dāl and with shadda, as a passive.
It is also read «دُورِسْتَ», without shadda and with wāw, as a passive, the wāw being substituted for the alif in دَارَسْتَ. It is also read with fatḥa on the dāl, the rāʾ and the sīn and sukūn on the tāʾ, i.e. "the signs have become effaced and wiped out".
It is read likewise but in the passive. It is also read دَرَسَ without tāʾ, the agent being the Prophet; and it is said: the Book, because of His saying «وَلِنُبَيِّنَهُ».

ukberi-tibyan:106-106.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (اتَّبِعْ مَا أُوحِيَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ) (١٠٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ رَبِّكَ): it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to أُوحِيَ; or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative object pronoun in أُوحِيَ; or a ḥāl from «مَا».
(لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ): it may be resumptive, or a ḥāl from رَبِّكَ, i.e. "from your Lord, being alone (in divinity)"; and it is a corroborative ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida).

ukberi-tibyan:107-107.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ مَا أَشْرَكُوا وَمَا جَعَلْنَاكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَفِيظًا وَمَا أَنْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِوَكِيلٍ) (١٠٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ): the object is omitted, i.e. "had Allah willed their faith".
And (جَعَلْنَاكَ) is transitive to two objects, and (حَفِيظًا) is the second. And (عَلَيْهِمْ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to حَفِيظًا, whose object is omitted, i.e. "and We have not made you one who keeps record of their deeds against them"; and this confirms the view of Sībawayh on giving government to the faʿīl pattern.

ukberi-tibyan:108-108.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تَسُبُّوا الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ فَيَسُبُّوا اللَّهَ عَدْوًا بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ كَذَلِكَ زَيَّنَّا لِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ عَمَلَهُمْ ثُمَّ إِلَى رَبِّهِمْ مَرْجِعُهُمْ فَيُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ) (١٠٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الَّذِينَ», or from the pronoun referring back to it.
(فَيَسُبُّوا): accusative as the answer to the prohibition; it is also said: it is jussive by conjunction, as in their saying لَا تُمَدِّدْهَا فَتُشَقِّقْهَا ("do not stretch it, and so tear it").
And (عَدْوًا): with fatḥa on the ʿayn and a light dāl; it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and on its accusative there are three views. First: it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). Second: a maṣdar not of the wording of the verb, because reviling is aggression in meaning.
Third: it is a maṣdar in the position of the ḥāl, and it is a corroborative ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida). It is also read with ḍamma on the ʿayn and the dāl and shadda on the wāw, a maṣdar on the pattern fuʿūl, like الْجُلُوس and الْقُعُود. It is also read with fatḥa on the ʿayn and with shadda; it is a singular with the meaning of a plural, i.e. "enemies", and it is a ḥāl.
(بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ): also a corroborative ḥāl. (كَذَلِكَ): in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "just as We made their deeds seem fair to every nation, We made their deeds seem fair to these".
